aiReview.summary: Official Google I/O 2024 workshop video on Gemini Cloud Assist and Code Assist for a Flask app on Cloud Run; useful as a GCP coding demo, not as Gemini Developer API documentation.
evidence: YouTube: Google Cloud Tech, uploaded 2024-05-16, duration 40:43, ~14K views.
Description names Gemini Cloud Assist, Code Assist, Python Flask, Serverless, Vertex AI, Codelab goo.gle/4b8YW4R.
Transcript covers Cloud Shell IDE, Cloud Run starter, explain/generate/inline Code Assist, GCS list_blobs example.
uncertainty: Whether the linked Codelab and console Gemini UX still match the video.
Exact Gemini API vs Vertex/Code Assist surface area beyond the description mention of Vertex AI.
aiReview.tagline: Workshop: AI coding assist for a serverless Flask app
aiReview.description: Watch a Google I/O workshop use in-console AI coding help to create, explain, and deploy a Python Flask app on serverless Cloud Run.
pros: Published by Google Cloud Tech from Google I/O 2024 with a linked Codelab.
Walks through enabling Gemini in Cloud Console and Cloud Shell IDE, code explanation, prompt-based generation, and inline suggestions.
Builds a Python Flask Cloud Run sample and notes that live-session cloud credits do not apply to the recording.
cons: Focuses on Gemini Code Assist / Cloud Assist in Google Cloud, not the Gemini Developer API or AI Studio client SDKs.
Interactive workshop format (credits, TAs, paper handouts) is less complete for viewers of the recording.
Content from May 2024 may lag current Gemini product names and console UX.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab on indexing private repos for Gemini Code Assist Enterprise customization via Developer Connect, .aiexclude, and gcloud indexes. Useful for Cloud IDE workflows, not the Gemini Developer API.
evidence: Title and URL: Code Customization with Gemini Code Assist Enterprise on codelabs.developers.google.com.
Meta description: Learn what’s new with Gemini Code Assist Enterprise for building with Google Cloud.
Steps use gcloud gemini code-repository-indexes, Developer Connect GitHub/GitLab links, and .aiexclude.
Prerequisites list Gemini Code Assist enabled, private repository, and IDE plugin.
uncertainty: Whether Code Assist Enterprise pricing and regional availability have changed since the lab was written.
Whether the sample GitHub/gcloud commands still match current CLI surface.
aiReview.tagline: Index private repos for tailored Code Assist completions
aiReview.description: Walk through Developer Connect, indexes, and .aiexclude so Code Assist Enterprise completions match your private codebase conventions.
pros: Official Google Codelab with step-by-step gcloud, Developer Connect, and IDE usage.
Covers .aiexclude, IAM for repository groups, and states private code is not used for broad training.
Includes an optional Spring Boot sample and links to IAM and data-governance docs.
cons: Targets Gemini Code Assist Enterprise on Google Cloud, not the Gemini Developer API or AI Studio.
Requires Code Assist entitlement, private repos, us-central1 or europe-west1, and indexing that can take up to 24 hours.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab on using Gemini in Google Cloud (logs, chat) to debug a failed Cloud Function deploy. Strong GCP tutorial quality, but it is Gemini for Google Cloud, not the Gemini Developer API.
evidence: canonicalUrl is developers.google.com Codelabs troubleshooting-with-gemini.
Meta description and intro state Gemini for Google Cloud for summarizing logs and explaining errors.
Steps use Cloud Functions, Logging, Explain this log entry, and Cloud Console chat, not generateContent or API keys.
Lab asks for Allow unauthenticated invocations and a billed GCP project.
uncertainty: Whether the Codelab UI still matches current Cloud Functions and Gemini Code Assist consoles.
Whether the directory is meant to include GCP Gemini product labs versus Developer API resources.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on GCP lab for AI-assisted log troubleshooting
aiReview.description: Walk through Cloud Function deploy failure, log explanation, and Gemini chat to find and fix the entry-point mismatch.
pros: Hosted as an official Google Codelabs guide with step-by-step console, logging, and Gemini prompts.
Covers log summarization, Explain this log entry, and follow-up troubleshooting questions.
Includes setup, a reproducible failed deploy, a working curl check, cleanup, and linked docs.
cons: Targets Gemini for Google Cloud observability, not the Gemini Developer API, SDKs, or AI Studio.
Requires a billed Google Cloud project and enabling multiple APIs.
Copy is slightly inconsistent (function name get_object_list vs get_order_list in later steps).

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab teaching Gemini Code Assist in Cloud Shell (chat, explain, generate, inline complete). Strong tutorial quality, but it targets Cloud IDE assistance rather than the Gemini Developer API.
evidence: Page title: A Tour of Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise for Developers in Google Cloud Shell Editor.
Meta description: Gemini Chat and inline assistance to generate and understand code in Google Cloud.
Lab steps include enabling Cloud Assist, Cloud Shell IDE, Python Flask Cloud Run template, GCS listing example.
Prerequisite: Cloud Project with billing and Gemini Code Assist enabled.
uncertainty: Whether the Duet AI-era lab is still fully current with Code Assist UI.
Exact commercial SKU/pricing of Code Assist Standard vs Enterprise.
Fit for a Gemini API-focused awesome list versus Google Cloud Code Assist.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on Cloud Shell tour of Code Assist coding features
aiReview.description: Use Cloud Shell IDE to chat, explain, generate, and complete code with Code Assist on a Python Cloud Run sample.
pros: Hosted on Google Codelabs with step-by-step Cloud Shell IDE setup.
Covers chat, code explanation, comment-driven generation, and inline suggestions on a Flask Cloud Run template.
States prerequisites including a billed Cloud project and Code Assist enabled.
cons: Does not cover the Gemini Developer API, SDKs, or AI Studio.
URL and some copy still use the former Duet AI name, which may confuse readers.
Requires Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise and Cloud billing, not a free API key path.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab that walks through Gemini for Cloud Help Me Write to generate Cloud Monitoring synthetic tests against a Cloud Run sample API. Useful GCP ops tutorial; not a Gemini Developer API or SDK guide.
evidence: canonicalUrl is a Google Codelabs page titled Writing Synthetic Monitoring Tests for your services using Gemini.
Meta description states use of Help Me Write to author Synthetic Monitoring Tests.
Lab steps enable Gemini for Cloud, deploy Cloud Run, and click HELP ME CODE in Synthetic Monitoring.
Reference section links cloud.google.com monitoring docs; no Gemini API client usage.
uncertainty: Last-updated date and whether Help Me Write UI still matches the screenshots.
Whether Code Assist / Cloud AI Companion API enablement still matches current product names.
aiReview.tagline: Codelab: generate Cloud Monitoring tests with Gemini
aiReview.description: Deploy a Cloud Run inventory API, then use Gemini Help Me Write to author Node.js synthetic monitors in Cloud Monitoring.
pros: Hosted on Google Codelabs with step-by-step console and Cloud Shell IDE instructions.
Covers enabling Gemini for Cloud, deploying a Flask inventory API on Cloud Run, and using Help Me Write for synthetic monitors.
Includes sample prompts, expected HTTP responses, and links to Cloud Monitoring and synthetic monitoring docs.
Content is licensed CC BY 4.0 with Apache 2.0 code samples.
cons: Targets Gemini for Cloud / Code Assist in GCP, not the Gemini Developer API.
Requires a billed Cloud project, Gemini Code Assist, and unauthenticated Cloud Run plus a Cloud Function.
Generated test code is non-deterministic and the lab does not pin model or SDK versions.

Content shows OpenAPI generation, Python Flask, Firestore sessions collection, Cloud Run
uncertainty: Whether the lab content is still current versus latest Code Assist UI and APIs
Exact commercial vs free Code Assist entitlement for all users
aiReview.tagline: Codelab: AI-assisted SDLC in Cloud Shell IDE
aiReview.description: Learn to design an OpenAPI spec, build a Flask app, generate tests, and deploy to Cloud Run using Gemini Code Assist.
pros: Hosted on Google Codelabs with step-by-step setup for Cloud Shell IDE and Gemini Code Assist.
Covers design (OpenAPI), Flask API and frontend generation, tests, and Cloud Run deploy.
Includes concrete prompts, sample OpenAPI, Firestore import, and Cloud Code template steps.
cons: Focuses on Gemini Code Assist and Google Cloud, not the Gemini Developer API or client SDKs.
Requires a billed Cloud project with Code Assist enabled, so it is not a zero-setup API tutorial.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab that walks through Vertex AI PDF summarization on Cloud Storage/BigQuery and using Gemini Code Assist in Cloud Shell IDE to explain and extend the Jump Start Solution. Useful for learning Code Assist, not a Gemini Developer API SDK.
evidence: canonical URL is developers.google.com/codelabs for gemini-code-assist-developer-aisummarization-jss
meta-description: Jump Start Solution uses Vertex AI to summarize PDFs in GCS; Code Assist used to understand and add functionality
Lab requires Chrome, Gmail, billed Cloud project, and Gemini Code Assist enabled
Steps include enabling Gemini for Cloud, Cloud Shell IDE, deploying generative-ai-document-summarization, explaining main.py, and prompting for Flask routes
uncertainty: Whether Code Assist UI names and Jump Start Solution remain current
Exact Gemini Code Assist SKU/pricing versus free trial for a given project
aiReview.tagline: Codelab: Code Assist on a Vertex AI summarizer
aiReview.description: Learn Vertex AI PDF summarization on GCP and use Code Assist in Cloud Shell to explain, generate, and extend a Flask upload app.
pros: Hosted on Google Codelabs with a clear step list, screenshots, and stated prerequisites.
Covers Code Assist chat, code explanation, generation, and a Flask GCS upload extension.
Ties to a documented Jump Start Solution using Vertex AI, Cloud Functions, GCS, and BigQuery.
cons: Targets Gemini Code Assist and Vertex AI on Google Cloud, not the consumer Gemini Developer API.
Needs a billed Cloud project and Code Assist enabled; Jump Start deploy can take ~15 minutes.
Sample generated code still uses a placeholder bucket name that the learner must replace.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab that walks through generating and running tests and fixing a Python app in Cloud Shell using Gemini Code Assist. Strong tutorial quality, but it targets the Cloud IDE assistant rather than the Gemini Developer API.
evidence: canonicalUrl is a Google Codelabs page titled Introduction to testing with Gemini Code Assist.
Meta description: Use Gemini Code Assist to help you write tests for your code.
Lab uses Cloud Shell Editor, Gemini Chat, unittest, and git clone of GoogleCloudPlatform/testing-with-duet-ai-codelab.
Prerequisites include a Cloud Project with billing and Gemini Code Assist enabled.
uncertainty: Whether the Duet AI enablement steps and sample repo still match current Cloud Code UI.
How well this fits a directory scoped strictly to Gemini API rather than Code Assist.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on lab for AI-assisted testing in Cloud Shell
aiReview.description: Use Cloud Shell Editor AI chat and inline help to generate unit tests, fix failures, and extend a Python web app.
pros: Hosted on Google Codelabs with a structured, step-by-step lab for beginners.
Shows chat and inline assistance for test generation, running unittest, and iterating on failing cases.
Pairs the lab with a public GoogleCloudPlatform sample repository.
States prerequisites (browser, Gmail, billed Cloud project, Code Assist enabled) clearly.
cons: Focuses on Gemini Code Assist in Cloud Shell, not the Gemini Developer API or SDKs.
Requires a billed Google Cloud project and product enablement, so it is not a no-setup API tutorial.
Copy still references Duet AI settings and a testing-with-duet-ai sample path, which may be dated.

aiReview.summary: Academic comparison paper on conversational models (including Gemini), not a Gemini API, SDK, or implementation resource. Weak fit for a developer directory.
evidence: canonicalUrl is a ResearchGate publication titled Grok, Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek Comparison and Applications in Conversational Artificial Intelligence.
Candidate type is web_url with title ResearchGate and no facts.readme or API docs.
Fetch of the publication page returned HTTP 403.
uncertainty: Peer-review status, authors, venue, and abstract could not be verified from the live page.
Whether the paper contains any Gemini API code or only product-level chat comparison.
aiReview.tagline: Academic comparison of conversational AI chat models
aiReview.description: Compares Grok, Gemini, ChatGPT, and DeepSeek for conversational AI applications rather than teaching Gemini API usage.
pros: Title indicates Gemini is one of several models compared in conversational AI.
Hosted as a citable ResearchGate publication rather than a marketing landing page.
cons: Does not document Gemini API, SDKs, or implementation patterns.
Full text could not be retrieved (HTTP 403), so methods and accuracy are unverified.
Discovered as a generic ResearchGate link from an unrelated awesome-grok list.

aiReview.summary: Official Google DeepMind product page for the Gemini model family, with capabilities, benchmarks, safety notes, and links to AI Studio and consumer chat. Useful as an About/overview resource, not as API or SDK documentation.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://deepmind.google/gemini redirects to https://deepmind.google/models/gemini/
Page title Gemini — Google DeepMind with Build with Gemini linking to aistudio.google.com
Repeated sourceEvidence from https://ai.google.dev/ with anchor text About
No riskFlags; bucket official-web
uncertainty: Current page content is Gemini 4 Argon-focused; older candidate title was only About
Pricing and API access details are not specified on this page
aiReview.tagline: Official DeepMind overview of frontier model capabilities
aiReview.description: Official DeepMind page covering model capabilities, benchmarks, safety, and ecosystem links for builders and users.
pros: Hosted on deepmind.google as the official model family landing page.
Linked from ai.google.dev as the About destination.
Includes capability, performance, safety, and ecosystem sections plus links to AI Studio and the consumer app.
cons: Marketing and model overview content rather than implementation or API reference.
Does not document SDKs, auth, or code samples for developers.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Gemini API documentation covering SDKs, REST, models, and agent workflows. Canonical developer reference for integrating Gemini.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs with title Gemini API | Google AI for Developers
meta-description: Gemini API Docs and API Reference
Get API key links to aistudio.google.com/apikey; Get Started at /gemini-api/docs/get-started
Code samples for Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, and REST interactions.create
uncertainty: Full site navigation beyond the landing page was not exhaustively audited
Commercial API pricing and quota details live on other pages
aiReview.tagline: Official API docs for models, SDKs, and agents
aiReview.description: Official developer docs for the Gemini API: get started, models, REST and SDK samples, tools, and agent workflows.
pros: Hosted on ai.google.dev as the canonical Gemini API docs and API reference.
Includes get-started paths, API key via AI Studio, and multi-language SDK plus REST examples.
Covers models, function calling, tools, Live API, and managed agents.
Linked from Google AI for Developers as the primary Docs entry.
cons: Page content and model names change frequently, so snippets can drift from older tutorials.
API usage itself is billed separately from the free documentation site.

aiReview.summary: Official Gemini API page stating Imagen is shut down and pointing developers to Nano Banana image models and generate_content. Useful as a migration notice, not as live Imagen implementation docs.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/imagen
Page states Imagen is shut down and no longer available in the Gemini API
Migration instructs gemini-2.5-flash-image / gemini-3.1-flash-image and client.models.generate_content
Last updated 2026-09-17 UTC per page footer
Meta description: Imagen models are shut down; migrate to Nano Banana for image generation
uncertainty: Whether Nano Banana naming and model IDs remain current beyond this page
Pricing of replacement image models is not specified on this page
aiReview.tagline: Official Imagen shutdown and Nano Banana migration notes
aiReview.description: States Imagen is unavailable in the Gemini API and lists model, method, and response changes for migrating image generation.
pros: Hosted on official Gemini API documentation at ai.google.dev.
Explicitly documents that Imagen models are shut down and no longer available.
Gives concrete migration mapping: model names, generate_content vs generate_images, and response parts.
Links to the current image generation guide for examples.
cons: The page is a deprecation notice, not working Imagen API reference or samples.
Title still reads as image generation with Imagen, which can mislead directory listings.
Implementation detail is thin beyond three migration bullets.

aiReview.summary: Official Google AI for Developers hub for Gemini API video generation, covering Omni Flash, Veo 3.1, and a link to video understanding. High-signal first-party docs suitable for an awesome list.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/video is official Google AI for Developers.
Page describes two generation models and links to /gemini-api/docs/omni, /veo, and /video-understanding.
Get API key points to AI Studio; cookbook is the google-gemini GitHub repo.
uncertainty: Exact API quotas, billing, and model availability over time are not fully specified on this hub page.
aiReview.tagline: Official guides for API video generation and editing
aiReview.description: Official docs comparing video generation models and linking to generation, conversational editing, and video understanding guides.
pros: First-party documentation on ai.google.dev for the Gemini API video surface.
Explains when to use Omni Flash versus Veo 3.1 and links to dedicated guides.
Points to video understanding for analysis of existing video rather than generation.
Last updated 2026-06-30 with CC BY 4.0 content licensing.
cons: This page is an overview hub rather than a full implementation cookbook.
Title in the candidate metadata is only “Docs”, which is uninformative without the URL.

aiReview.summary: Official Android developer documentation for on-device generative AI via ML Kit GenAI APIs and AICore. High-quality, maintained Google docs suitable for a Gemini developer directory.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://developer.android.com/ai/gemini-nano on developer.android.com
Page states Gemini Nano runs in Android AICore with ML Kit GenAI high-level APIs
Linked from ai.google.dev curated readme as Gemini Nano on Android
Safety and privacy sections reference Private Compute Core and request isolation
uncertainty: Device availability and feature coverage across OEM hardware not verified here
ML Kit GenAI API versioning and breaking changes over time not audited
aiReview.tagline: On-device GenAI APIs for Android apps
aiReview.description: Use ML Kit GenAI APIs and AICore to run summarization, rewriting, and other tasks locally without sending data to the cloud.
pros: Official Android Developers documentation last updated 2026-10-08 UTC.
Covers ML Kit GenAI APIs for prompt, summarization, proofreading, rewriting, image description, and speech recognition.
Documents AICore privacy model, Private Compute Core isolation, and on-device inference architecture.
Links hybrid inference via Firebase AI Logic when on-device limits apply.
Includes an Android skill install command for the ML Kit Prompt API.
cons: Focuses on Android on-device APIs rather than the cloud Gemini Developer API.
Device hardware, token limits, and model capability constraints are inherent to the approach.

aiReview.summary: Official Android Developers hub for IDE-native Gemini/AI agent features in Android Studio, including docs links, model/key options, and individual vs enterprise plans. Strong official documentation signal; it is IDE assistance more than a standalone Gemini API SDK.
evidence: Page title and canonical: AI in Android Studio at https://developer.android.com/ai-in-android.
Linked from ai.google.dev curated readme as Android Studio.
Compare offerings: No cost individual plan with limited Gemini/Gemma quota; Google AI Pro/Ultra; Gemini Enterprise with Cloud ToS.
Feature docs linked: /studio/gemini/overview, agent-mode, android-skills, generate-compose-previews.
uncertainty: Exact current quota numbers and regional availability were not verified beyond the landing page.
Whether all listed skills require a specific Studio version was not independently tested.
aiReview.tagline: IDE-native AI agent for Android app development
aiReview.description: Build, debug, and profile Android apps with an IDE agent, Compose tools, and optional Gemini, third-party, or local models.
pros: Hosted on developer.android.com with links to feature docs such as agent mode and Compose preview generation.
Documents Gemini included on login, bring-your-own API keys (including Google AI Studio), and local models via Gemma, Ollama, or LM Studio.
Lists concrete Android-specific capabilities: Compose UI tools, Logcat/Gradle/crash context, emulator validation, and Journeys tests.
States individual no-cost access with limited quota plus Google AI Pro/Ultra and Gemini Enterprise options.
cons: The listed URL redirects to /ai-in-android and is product marketing plus docs entry, not a Gemini REST/SDK reference.
Quota, availability, and enterprise rollout details are plan-dependent and not fully specified on the landing page.

aiReview.summary: Official Google AI docs page describing how researchers can use the Gemini API (generation controls, multimodal and long-context features) and apply for academic API credits.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-for-research
Page title and H1: Accelerate discovery with Gemini for Research
Links to generate-content, vision, long-context, available-regions, AI Studio API key, and Google Form application
Code samples use google-genai / generativelanguage.googleapis.com generateContent
uncertainty: Current Academic Program acceptance rates, credit amounts, and whether the Google Form is still open
Whether Java/Go snippets on the live page match the latest SDK APIs
aiReview.tagline: Official research guide and academic API credit program
aiReview.description: Explains research uses of the Gemini API, shows starter snippets, and outlines eligibility for academic credits and higher rate limits.
pros: Hosted on ai.google.dev under Gemini API docs with last-updated date 2026-09-23.
Covers generation analysis/control, multimodal inputs, long context, and AI Studio/API access.
Includes starter generate-content examples in Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, and REST.
Documents the Gemini Academic Program: eligibility, research areas of interest, and a public apply form.
cons: Credits and higher limits are discretionary, country-limited, and reviewed monthly rather than guaranteed.
Page mixes high-level research pitch with snippets; it is not a full API reference.
Featured academic quotes are anecdotal and not reproducible tutorials.

Official Zero plugins — give your AI agent the ability to discover and pay for
new capabilities.

Zero is a search engine and payment layer for AI agents. With the Zero plugin
installed, your agent can find capabilities it doesn't have built in — image,
video, and audio generation, web scraping, real-time data, messaging, and
more — call them, and pay per use from a single wallet. No per-service
signups, no API keys to manage.

you through setup. Just paste this to your agent:

Help me set up Zero — a tool that lets you find and use extra services you

hosting a free webpage). It's free to set up.

Set it up by running the Zero CLI's setup (needs Node.js — install it first if
`npm` isn't available):

    zero auth login

reference.excerpt:
# Gemini API skills

A library of skills for the Gemini API, SDK and model interactions.

## About

LLMs have fixed knowledge, being trained at a specific point in time. Software
dev is fast paced and changes often, where new libraries are launched every day
and best practices evolve quickly.

This leaves a knowledge gap that language models can't solve on their own. For
example, models don't know about themselves when they're trained, and they
aren't necessarily aware of subtle changes in best practices (like [thought
circulation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures)) or SDK
changes.

[Skills](https://agentskills.io/) are a lightweight technique for adding
relevant context to your agents. This repo contains skills related to building
apps powered by the Gemini API.

### Performance

Our evaluations found that adding this skill improved an agent's ability to
generate correct API code following best practices to 87% with Gemini 3 Flash
and 96% with Gemini 3.1 Pro. F

README install: gemini extension install https://github.com/thoreinstein/gemini-beads
Commands include /beads:prime, ready, create, list, show, update, close, sync.
MIT license file present; topics include gemini-cli-extension and google-gemini.
uncertainty: Live activity, last-commit date, and whether bd API coverage stays current.
Runtime safety of hooks wrapping arbitrary bd commands.
Exact Beads version compatibility.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension for graph-based, git-backed task memory
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that wraps Beads (bd) so sessions can track issues, dependencies, and project context in git.
pros: Documented as a Gemini CLI extension with gemini extension install and gemini-extension.json.
README lists slash commands, mapped bd subcommands, and GEMINI.md agent workflow.
MIT license; issues/state are described as stored in git via Beads.
Listed in awesome-gemini-cli and awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
cons: Requires a separate Beads (bd) CLI on PATH; this repo is a thin wrapper.
Only ~26 stars, 3 forks, and 10 commits, so maintenance depth is limited.
Does not implement the Gemini API itself; it targets Gemini CLI workflows.

aiReview.summary: Apache-2.0 Gemini CLI / Antigravity plugin for spec-driven development with agents; useful for coding workflows but not a Gemini API SDK.
evidence: GitHub description: plugin for AI coding agents enabling Spec-Driven Development.
README installation uses agy plugins install and ~/.gemini/config/plugins/.
License listed as Apache-2.0; topics include gemini and spec-driven-development.
uncertainty: Latest commit date and release cadence not confirmed from the truncated page.
Runtime behavior and safety of skills/rules were not executed.
Degree of first-party Google vs community ownership of gemini-cli-extensions is not verified.
aiReview.tagline: Spec-driven plugin for AI coding agents
aiReview.description: Install a plugin that makes coding agents specify, plan, then implement features via managed project context.
pros: Public GitHub repo under gemini-cli-extensions with Apache-2.0 license, README, CONTRIBUTING, and plugin.json.
Documents install/uninstall for Antigravity (agy plugins / ~/.gemini plugins) and Claude Code marketplace install.
Describes a Context → Spec & Plan → Implement workflow with rules and skills directories.
Maintenance signals include ~3.8k stars, ~299 forks, and 133 commits on main.
cons: Targets agent plugins (Antigravity, Claude Code) rather than the Gemini Developer API itself.
README install paths mix Antigravity, Gemini plugin dirs, and Claude Code, which may confuse directory listing.
Quality of generated specs/plans depends on the host agent and is not independently verified here.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that adds listen-mode commands so the CLI can run as a server. README is a one-line install; implementation depth and security of the listen server are not documented.
evidence: GitHub description: Turn Gemini-CLI into a server with /isten commands packaged as a Gemini-CLI extension.
Install command uses gemini extensions install against the GitHub repo.
Apache-2.0 license listed on the repo.
14 stars, 2 forks, 9 commits on main.
uncertainty: Actual listen-server implementation quality and authentication.
Maintenance cadence beyond 9 commits.
Whether /isten is a typo or the real command name.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension that exposes listen-mode server command
aiReview.description: Installs as a Gemini CLI extension so you can run listen-mode commands and treat the CLI as a local server.
pros: Packaged as a Gemini CLI extension with a documented git install URL.
Apache-2.0 license is present.
Repository includes gemini-extension.json plus commands, scripts, and servers directories.
cons: README has almost no usage, API, or security documentation.
Only 9 commits, 14 stars, and no releases shown.
Listen-mode server behavior is not explained, so operational risk is hard to assess.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that captures desktop frames or streams them via MCP and slash commands. Small Apache-2.0 repo with a thin README; screen capture implies privacy risk.
evidence: GitHub description: share screen with Gemini-CLI using MCP and custom slash commands.
README install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/automateyournetwork/GeminiCLI_ScreenShare_Extension.git
Repo layout includes commands/screenshare, servers/, GEMINI.md, gemini-extension.json, Apache-2.0 LICENSE.
Stats: 21 stars, 4 forks, 14 commits, public, not a fork.
uncertainty: Actual MCP tool behavior, OS support, and data sent to Gemini not verified from source.
Maintenance cadence and issue/PR activity not inspected.
No facts.readme excerpt was provided in the candidate payload.
aiReview.tagline: Capture or stream the desktop into Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that exposes screen capture and streaming through MCP and custom slash commands.
pros: Official Gemini CLI install path via gemini extensions install from GitHub.
Apache-2.0 licensed public repo with gemini-extension.json, MCP servers, and slash-command files.
Stated purpose is single-frame capture and streaming modes for Gemini CLI.
cons: README is essentially install plus one-line purpose; little usage or security guidance.
Only 14 commits, 21 stars, and no releases listed.
Desktop capture/streaming can leak secrets on screen without documented consent or redaction controls.

aiReview.summary: Open-source Gemini CLI extension that wires Cisco pyATS to Gemini CLI via a testbed.yaml path; thin README and modest GitHub traction, but clearly on-topic for Gemini CLI extensions.
evidence: Repo description: An easy to install pyATS extension for Gemini CLI.
Install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/automateyournetwork/pyATS_GeminiCLI_Extension.git
Requires export PYATS_TESTBED_PATH and customizing servers/testbed.yaml.
Apache-2.0 license; files include servers/, GEMINI.md, gemini-extension.json.
Listed as pyATS in awesome-gemini-cli and awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
uncertainty: Exact MCP/server capabilities and pyATS commands exposed were not fully inspected beyond README.
Last-commit date and CI/test coverage not verified from the HTML overview.
Safety of executing network commands via the extension against live devices is not documented.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension that enables Cisco pyATS testbeds
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that connects pyATS using PYATS_TESTBED_PATH and a customizable testbed.yaml.
pros: Public GitHub repo with Apache-2.0 license and gemini-extension.json plus GEMINI.md.
Documents gemini extensions install from the GitHub URL and PYATS_TESTBED_PATH.
Includes a default testbed.yaml aimed at the DevNet CML sandbox.
59 commits, 10 stars, and 4 forks indicate some ongoing activity.
cons: README is very short (install plus testbed note) with little API, security, or troubleshooting detail.
Low community traction and no releases listed on the repo page.
Users must replace testbed.yaml; network credentials and device access are implied but not documented for safe handling.

aiReview.summary: Small Gemini CLI extension that exposes IPv4 CIDR subnet math via MCP slash commands. Docs are a one-line install plus GEMINI.md; the repo is tiny and not a Gemini API SDK.
evidence: GitHub description: An extension for GeminiCLI that performs subnet calculation.
gemini-extension.json registers mcpServers.subnetcalculator via bash servers/run.sh and contextFileName GEMINI.md.
GEMINI.md documents subnet_calculator(cidr) and /subnet:* slash commands for IPv4 CIDR.
Listed in Piebald-AI awesome-gemini-cli / extensions as Subnet calculator.
uncertainty: Correctness of the subnet implementation and run.sh MCP server was not executed.
Last commit date and ongoing maintenance beyond 6 commits on main were not verified in detail.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI MCP tools for IPv4 CIDR math
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that calculates IPv4 subnet details, hosts, masks, and next network via MCP slash commands.
pros: Apache-2.0 Gemini CLI extension with gemini-extension.json, MCP server, and GEMINI.md command mapping.
Defines slash commands for calc, hosts, next, masks, and help plus explicit CIDR validation rules.
Install is a single gemini extensions install from the public GitHub URL.
cons: README is only a title, one-sentence description, and install line with no usage examples or tests.
Repository shows 5 stars, 0 forks, and 6 commits, so maintenance signal is weak.
Scope is Gemini CLI tooling, not the Gemini Developer API or client SDKs.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension for packet-capture analysis via RAG, MCP, and slash commands; relevant but README is a stub and install is labeled future-facing.
evidence: GitHub description and README: RAG, MCP, custom slash commands for packet captures.
Repo files: GEMINI.md, gemini-extension.json, commands/packet_buddy, servers; Apache-2.0 license.
66 commits on main; install snippet uses gemini extensions install.
uncertainty: Code quality, MCP server behavior, and capture-data handling were not audited.
Whether gemini extensions install currently works as documented.
Maintenance cadence beyond commit count and star count.
aiReview.tagline: Analyze packet captures from Gemini CLI with RAG and MCP
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that uses RAG, MCP, and custom slash commands to analyze packet captures.
pros: Public Apache-2.0 GitHub repo structured as a Gemini CLI extension (gemini-extension.json, commands, servers).
Stated purpose is packet-capture analysis using RAG, MCP, and custom slash commands.
Includes an install command targeting gemini extensions install and GOOGLE_API_KEY usage.
cons: README is a stub: install is marked “in the future” with no usage, architecture, or safety notes.
Low community signal (about 20 stars, 1 fork) and no releases listed on the repo page.
Does not document how captures are handled or what MCP servers execute.

aiReview.summary: VS Code extension that launches Gemini CLI (plus Claude, Codex, and Qwen) in editor tabs and broadcasts prompts across them. Modest GitHub traction and hype-heavy docs; useful as a Gemini CLI companion, not an API SDK.
evidence: GitHub description and README: MAGUS Council multi-CLI VS Code integration for Gemini CLI, Claude, Codex, Qwen.
Prerequisites: npm install -g @google/gemini-cli plus other CLIs.
MIT license, src/, docs/, CHANGELOG, unit/integration vscode-test configs.
~16 stars, 7 forks, public repo d3j/gemini-cli-on-vscode.
uncertainty: Marketplace install counts and last-commit recency not fully verified from the page snapshot.
Runtime security of CLI spawning and history folder not audited.
Whether GPT-5/Codex naming matches current OpenAI products.
aiReview.tagline: Run multiple AI CLIs as VS Code editor tabs
aiReview.description: Launch Gemini, Claude, Codex, and Qwen CLIs in editor panes and broadcast one prompt to all of them from VS Code.
pros: Open-source MIT VS Code extension that wraps Google Gemini CLI in editor tabs rather than only a terminal panel.
Supports launching Gemini, Claude, Codex, and Qwen CLIs and broadcasting a single prompt to multiple CLIs.
Repo includes tests, changelog, Japanese README, and documented prerequisites for installing each CLI.
cons: Low adoption signals (about 16 stars, 7 forks, 33 commits) relative to the marketing claims.
Depends on separately installed third-party CLIs and their account auth, not the Gemini API SDK.
README uses exaggerated claims (e.g. “world’s first”, GPT-5) that are hard to verify.

aiReview.summary: Community Gemini CLI slash commands that start a local HTTP listener (port 8765) so curl, ngrok, or Slack can send events into the CLI, including optional Slack Bolt and MCP use. Small Apache-2.0 repo with thin docs; exposing the listener via a public tunnel is a security tradeoff.
evidence: GitHub description: A /listen feature for Gemini CLI.
README documents /listen:* commands, MCP note, Slack/ngrok usage, and Slack Bolt env vars.
Repo shows Apache-2.0, commands/listen, scripts, slack_bolt, 21 stars, 9 forks, 26 commits.
uncertainty: Listener implementation quality, auth on port 8765, and Whisper transcription behavior were not audited in code.
Maintenance cadence and compatibility with current Gemini CLI versions are unverified.
aiReview.tagline: HTTP listener slash commands for Gemini CLI events
aiReview.description: Adds /listen commands so Gemini CLI accepts HTTP events locally, with optional Slack Bolt, ngrok testing, and MCP access.
pros: Provides Gemini CLI /listen start, status, stop, logs, health, help, clear, and live commands.
Documents curl/ngrok POST testing and Slack slash-command or Slack Bolt integration.
States MCP servers already configured in Gemini CLI remain usable when messages arrive.
Licensed Apache-2.0 with a public GitHub repository.
cons: Installation is a manual copy of commands and scripts into ~/.gemini.
README is informal, has typos, and embeds a sample ngrok URL in the curl example.
Public tunneling of a local CLI listener plus Slack bot tokens raises exposure risk.
Low activity signals (about 21 stars, 9 forks, 26 commits) and no documented test suite.

aiReview.summary: A small GitHub collection of Gemini CLI custom slash-command TOML files for productivity and coding tasks, with a README install path. Single-commit repo; treat as examples, not a maintained product.
evidence: GitHub README lists /photo-rename, /report-gen, /email-draft, /test-gen, /debug-assistant, /security-audit, and related commands.
About 167 stars and 15 forks; public repo amitkmaraj/gemini-cli-custom-slash-commands.
Layout is .gemini/commands plus README; npm install -g @google/gemini-cli@latest in quick start.
uncertainty: Actual TOML prompt contents and shell side effects were not fully reviewed file-by-file.
License and ongoing updates after the single commit are not confirmed.
Whether security-audit/cleanup commands are safe to run on real trees is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: TOML slash-command pack for Gemini CLI workflows
aiReview.description: Copy project or user-scoped .gemini command files for photo rename, reports, email, tests, debug, and similar CLI tasks.
pros: Documents ten Gemini CLI custom slash commands with usage examples.
Points to copying .gemini/commands for project- or user-scoped setup.
Cites the Google Cloud post on Gemini CLI custom slash commands as inspiration.
cons: Repository history shows a single commit, so maintenance is unverified.
README “official docs” link targets gcloud custom-jobs, not Gemini CLI slash-command docs.
Commands that organize files, audit security, or generate tests depend on prompt quality and are not independently audited here.

aiReview.summary: Archived MIT TypeScript CLI/orchestration project that wraps Gemini CLI, Google AI services, and multi-agent workflows; relevant historically but no longer maintained as of 2026-01-29.
evidence: GitHub banner: archived by owner on Jan 29, 2026.
About: Claude-Flow translated to Gemini CLI; autonomous AI development team.
README: npm @clduab11/gemini-flow, gemini extensions install, A2A+MCP, 66 agents.
License MIT; ~386 stars, 66 forks, 94 commits.
uncertainty: Whether npm package still installs and works against current Gemini CLI.
Accuracy of claimed SQLite ops/sec and Google-service coverage.
Security review of agent execution paths not performed.
aiReview.tagline: Archived multi-agent CLI for Gemini and Google AI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension and agent swarm CLI that coordinates Google AI services via A2A and MCP. Project is archived.
pros: Public GitHub repo with MIT license, npm package, docs, Docker, and Gemini CLI extension files.
Explicit Gemini CLI / Google Gemini topics and Vertex AI setup docs.
Community signals include hundreds of stars and dozens of forks before archive.
cons: Owner archived the repository as read-only on 2026-01-29 and states Google Antigravity makes the project unnecessary.
README is marketing-heavy with extreme performance claims that are hard to verify.
Autonomous agent/hive-mind tooling plus live-demo links raise maintenance and operational risk for a directory listing.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Gemini CLI extension that bridges a local ACP agent to Discord with documented boss/guest auth, multimodal attachments, and MCP Discord tools. Small community signals (few stars) and host-side privileges (admin actions, local media search) warrant a careful look before listing.
evidence: GitHub description and README: Discord bridge for Gemini CLI / ACP; gemini extensions install URL.
Topics include gemini-cli, gemini-cli-extension, gemini-api, typescript, mcp.
103 commits, tests/, vitest.config.ts, docs/, gemini-extension.json, MIT LICENSE.
Permission model: BOSS vs GUEST; guests cannot use MCP/shell/filesystem by default.
uncertainty: Runtime security of token storage and daemon process isolation not audited.
Test coverage quality and CI pass status not independently verified.
Maintenance cadence beyond commit count and README freshness not assessed.
aiReview.tagline: Discord bridge for a local Gemini CLI agent
aiReview.description: Connect Gemini CLI ACP sessions to Discord DMs and channels with local credentials, slash commands, and Discord MCP tools.
pros: Installs as a Gemini CLI extension using ACP mode and optional Vertex AI or GEMINI_API_KEY auth.
README documents Discord bot setup, boss-only privileged commands, guest restrictions, and fail-closed authority on DISCORD_BOSS_USER_ID.
Repository includes tests, TypeScript source, CI workflows, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, and MIT license.
Supports multimodal Discord attachments and MCP tools for messaging, history, cron, and admin actions.
cons: GitHub popularity is low (about 5 stars and 3 forks).
The bot can kick/timeout users, search host media, and run unattended with a local API key, increasing operational exposure if misconfigured.
Requires Node.js 22+, a Discord bot with privileged intents, and non-interactive Gemini credentials.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Gemini CLI extension that requires declared intent plans and ArmorIQ backend policy checks before tool use; useful for CLI security but depends on a third-party API, a curl|bash installer, and fail-closed behavior without a key.
evidence: GitHub description and README: intent-based security plugin for Gemini CLI with register_intent_plan MCP tool.
README status v0.3.2; MIT license; 32 commits; 4 stars; gemini-cli-extension topic.
Installer and ARMORIQ_API_KEY / credentials.json documented; hooks deny if not configured.
uncertainty: Whether ArmorIQ backend usage is free, paid, or quota-limited beyond needing an API key.
Effectiveness of enforcement against real Gemini CLI bypasses was not independently verified.
Long-term maintenance given low community metrics.
aiReview.tagline: Intent-plan checks for Gemini CLI tool calls
aiReview.description: Adds Gemini CLI hooks and an MCP server so tool calls match a declared plan and ArmorIQ policy before they run.
pros: Public GitHub repo documents Gemini CLI hooks, MCP tools, and a fail-closed unconfigured mode.
Includes tests, changelog, MIT license, and gemini-extension.json for CLI integration.
Explains local drift checks versus backend policy and lists env vars for timeout, TTL, and credentials.
cons: Requires an ArmorIQ API key and posts enforce/audit traffic to api.armoriq.ai.
Primary install is curl piped to bash writing global Gemini settings.
Repository is early (v0.3.x, few stars, zero forks) so maintenance and security claims are lightly proven.

aiReview.summary: Generated Gemini CLI extension that records and recalls team decision memory via a local kg engine; relevant but early-stage (few commits, 1 star) and installs prebuilt binaries to ~/.kgai.
evidence: GitHub description: Gemini CLI extension generated from kgaidev/kgai; shared decision memory.
Install snippet: gemini extensions install https://github.com/kgaidev/kgai-gemini
States personal Google login is ineligible; GEMINI_API_KEY from AI Studio required.
MIT license listed on the repo.
uncertainty: Runtime quality of hooks, skills, and kg binary not verified from source review.
Whether kgai.dev or the parent repo is the canonical support channel.
Actual Gemini API surface usage beyond CLI extension packaging.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension for shared coding decision memory
aiReview.description: Install as a Gemini CLI extension so the agent records, recalls, and syncs code decisions across a team.
pros: Official install path is gemini extensions install against this GitHub URL.
README documents GEMINI_API_KEY from AI Studio and slash commands /kg-ask, /kg-decision, /kg-history.
MIT-licensed and explicitly generated from kgaidev/kgai with GEMINI.md and gemini-extension.json present.
Topics include gemini-cli-extension and knowledge-graph.
cons: Repository has only 3 commits, 1 star, and 0 forks, so maintenance is weakly evidenced.
First session installs a prebuilt kg engine to ~/.kgai (Linux/macOS; Windows via WSL).
Issues and source are deferred to the parent kgaidev/kgai repo rather than this generated package.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that blocks agent stop until real tests/lint/typecheck pass, wrapping the isitdone hook via npx. Small MIT repo with clear install docs, low adoption, and core logic living in a sibling package.
evidence: GitHub description and README: Gemini CLI extension packaging isitdone hooks.
Install command: gemini extensions install https://github.com/raimondasl/isitdone-gemini.
Hook table: AfterAgent * with 600s timeout; AfterTool write_file|replace 30s.
MIT license listed on the repository.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README.
uncertainty: Cannot independently verify @aivolution/isitdone package quality or supply-chain from this repo alone.
Maintenance cadence and issue/PR activity not fully visible from the listing snapshot.
Hook behavior against current Gemini CLI extension API versions not executed here.
aiReview.tagline: Block Gemini CLI stop until tests actually pass
aiReview.description: Installs AfterAgent and AfterTool hooks so Gemini CLI cannot claim done until repo tests, lint, and typecheck pass.
pros: README documents install via gemini extensions install, hook events, timeouts, and claim-gated test runs.
States no API keys, network, telemetry, or extra dependencies beyond npx @aivolution/isitdone.
MIT license; includes gemini-extension.json, hooks, and an isitdone skill.
Supports detecting checks from common manifests and optional .isitdone.json.
cons: Only 1 star, 0 forks, 11 commits, and no GitHub releases.
Runtime depends on downloading @aivolution/isitdone via npx rather than shipping the checker in-repo.
README notes it was built by Claude as an experiment in agent-driven open source.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that wires a hosted GTD MCP server, GEMINI.md prompts, and /gtd:* slash commands. Docs are clear, but the repo is config-only with two commits, one star, and paid SaaS behind OAuth.
evidence: GitHub description and README: Gemini CLI extension, hosted MCP at mcp.gtdbrain.com, GEMINI.md, /gtd:* commands.
Install command: gemini extensions install https://github.com/minosin/gtdbrain-gemini-extension.
Pricing section: new email creates free account; handful of free tool actions then subscription.
MIT LICENSE listed; 1 star, 0 forks, 2 commits on master.
uncertainty: Cannot verify MCP server security, OAuth implementation, or tool behavior from this config repo.
Exact subscription prices not listed in the README.
Cannot verify real-time sync with web/iOS/Android or Telegram bot quality.
aiReview.tagline: GTD board via Gemini CLI MCP tools and slash commands
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that connects to a hosted MCP GTD board, with capture, review, and context slash commands.
pros: README documents install, /mcp auth OAuth, slash commands, and 16 MCP tool names.
Extension is MIT-licensed configuration (gemini-extension.json, GEMINI.md, commands) with no local runtime code claimed.
States cards cannot be deleted via Gemini and links privacy/terms and uninstall.
cons: Repository has two commits, one star, and zero forks, so maintenance is weakly evidenced.
Ongoing tool use requires a GTD Brain subscription after a small free trial.
Task data and MCP execution live on a third-party hosted server, not in this repo.

aiReview.summary: Small Apache-2.0 Docker wrapper that runs Gemini CLI in an isolated container with project-mounted files, optional preseed config, and Context7 notes. Useful as a convenience wrapper, but the repo is tiny (few stars/commits) and docs do not show deep API or maintenance signals.
evidence: GitHub description: Gemini Dockerized CLI with small improvements.
README documents docker run --rm -it -v ./:/app/ hlpr/gdcli and alias gdcli.
Features listed: Context7 integration, llm/PROJECT.md, /preseed/ mount, CONTEXT7_API_KEY.
License badge Apache-2.0; 4 stars, 0 forks, 10 commits on main.
uncertainty: Image hlpr/gdcli contents, update cadence, and whether it tracks official Gemini CLI releases.
Actual security properties of the container (user, capabilities, network) are not verified from the Dockerfile.
Maintenance activity beyond commit count is unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Isolated Docker wrapper for running Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Run Gemini CLI in a container with project mounts, optional preseed config, and Context7 settings for a safer local workflow.
pros: Wraps Gemini CLI in Docker with a documented one-line docker run and alias.
Apache-2.0 license is present on the repository.
README covers init of ./llm/.gemini.store, custom preseed mounts, and CONTEXT7_API_KEY.
Positions isolation as a way to limit unintended host-side CLI actions.
cons: Very small project: 4 stars, 0 forks, about 10 commits, no releases.
Documentation is brief and does not specify Gemini API versions or upstream CLI compatibility.
Mounts the current directory into the container, so isolation is not a full sandbox of project files.

aiReview.summary: Community Docker wrapper for Google’s Gemini CLI with documented mounts, UID/GID mapping, Node and Bun images, and CI-built tags. Useful packaging, not an official SDK or API client.
evidence: GitHub description: Gemini CLI wrapped as a Docker image without installing Node.
README links google-gemini/gemini-cli and Docker Hub tgagor/gemini-cli.
Topics include gemini-cli; Node and Bun Dockerfiles plus build workflow present.
uncertainty: Current Docker Hub pull counts and image provenance beyond README badges.
Whether images track every upstream Gemini CLI release without lag.
aiReview.tagline: Run Gemini CLI in Docker without installing Node.js
aiReview.description: Wraps Gemini CLI in Node and Bun Docker images with workspace mounts, config persistence, and multi-arch tags.
pros: Packages the official Gemini CLI so users can avoid a local Node.js install.
Documents a shell function for workspace, ~/.gemini, TTY, and UID/GID mapping.
Offers Node (amd64/arm64/armv7) and Bun image variants with versioned tags.
Repo shows 160 commits, GitHub Actions build badge, and GPL-2.0 license.
cons: Third-party image; users must trust the publisher for CLI binaries and updates.
GitHub popularity is modest (about 19 stars, 4 forks).
macOS permission/performance caveats are noted in the README.

aiReview.summary: The listed title points at a small Gemini CLI JSON-to-HTML log script nested in a much larger MIT-licensed puzzle/skills repo, so the canonical URL is a poor match for a dedicated CLI tool listing.
evidence: awesome-gemini-cli lists the repo as Gemini CLI Logs Prettifier.
Repo description: Ideas, tricks, materials with puzzles for AIs and some wetware; 17 stars, 2 forks, MIT.
Folder code/Gemini CLI logs prettifier with pretty_print_chat.py and README for ~/.gemini/tmp HTML conversion.
uncertainty: Windows path portability and script maintenance cadence were not independently verified.
Whether the listing should target the nested folder versus the whole repo.
aiReview.tagline: Turn Gemini CLI JSON session files into readable HTML
aiReview.description: Converts Gemini CLI logs, checkpoints, and sessions under ~/.gemini/tmp into interlinked HTML for local browsing and debugging.
pros: A Python script in code/Gemini CLI logs prettifier converts Gemini CLI JSON logs and checkpoints into HTML.
The parent repository is public, MIT-licensed, and actively committed.
README documents Gemini.md memory files and Gemini CLI skills/MCP alignment.
cons: The canonical GitHub URL is a broad puzzles-and-cognition project, not a standalone logs-prettifier package.
The prettifier is a nested helper with limited stars/forks at the repo level and no separate release.
README includes local file:// skill links and speculative agent-automation content unrelated to the listing title.

aiReview.summary: Python SDK wrapping Gemini CLI with a Claude Code SDK-compatible query API; experimental, pip-installable, but the GitHub repo is archived and read-only as of Sep 15, 2026.
evidence: GitHub about: Python SDK for Gemini CLI - API-compatible with Claude Code SDK.
Public archive banner: archived by the owner on Sep 15, 2026.
README: pip install gemini-cli-sdk; requires Gemini CLI and API key; 18 stars, 3 forks, MIT license.
uncertainty: Whether a successor fork exists after archival.
PyPI package health and last published version versus the archived tree.
Runtime safety of spawning Gemini CLI and extra LLM parsing.
aiReview.tagline: Python wrapper for Gemini CLI with Claude SDK-like API
aiReview.description: Programmatically query Gemini CLI from Python with Claude Code SDK-compatible imports, options, and async message streaming.
pros: Provides a Python query() API over Gemini CLI with Claude Code SDK-compatible imports and aliases.
Documents installation, prerequisites, examples, architecture, migration, tests, and known limitations.
MIT-licensed open-source package installable via pip as gemini-cli-sdk.
cons: Repository is archived and read-only as of Sep 15, 2026, so it is no longer maintained.
README marks the project experimental with an evolving API and remaining feature gaps.
SDK still relies on LLM parsing rather than native JSON in the documented migration path.
