aiReview.summary: Community Vercel AI SDK provider that routed Gemini through Gemini CLI OAuth/Code Assist; the repo is archived and the package is deprecated after Google stopped serving Gemini CLI individual-account requests.
evidence: GitHub about: community Vercel AI SDK provider for Gemini CLI via Gemini Code Assist license.
README warning: package deprecated; Google transitioned Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI and stopped individual-account CLI requests on 2026-06-18.
Public archive banner; ~72 stars, 18 forks, MIT license, Node >= 20 badges.
uncertainty: Current npm download counts and last publish date not independently verified.
Whether remaining api-key/Vertex modes still function versus first-party providers.
Historical compliance of Code Assist OAuth reuse for SDK workloads.
aiReview.tagline: Vercel AI SDK access via Gemini CLI OAuth
aiReview.description: Use Gemini models from the Vercel AI SDK through Gemini CLI auth and Cloud Code endpoints. Archived after the CLI path ended.
pros: README documents AI SDK v4–v6 version mapping, install, OAuth and API-key auth, and a generateText quick start.
Repository includes TypeScript source, tests (vitest), examples, changelog, MIT license, and CI workflows.
Deprecation notice points users to official @ai-sdk/google and @ai-sdk/google-vertex providers.
cons: GitHub marks the repository as archived (read-only) and npm versions as deprecated.
Core oauth-personal use case no longer works after Gemini CLI individual-account serving stopped in June 2026.
Community provider, not an official Google or Vercel first-party SDK.

aiReview.summary: Open-source FastAPI proxy that exposes Gemini CLI OAuth credentials as OpenAI-compatible and native Gemini HTTP APIs, including Docker deploy. High ToS/quota-circumvention risk because it is framed around using Google’s free Gemini CLI quota via unofficial endpoints.
evidence: README title: Gemini CLI to API Proxy; FastAPI server converting Gemini CLI into OpenAI-compatible and native Gemini APIs.
Explicit claim: leverage Google's free Gemini API quota through familiar OpenAI interfaces.
590 stars, 626 forks, 57 commits, MIT license, Dockerfile and docker-compose present.
Auth via GEMINI_AUTH_PASSWORD plus GEMINI_CREDENTIALS JSON with client_id, client_secret, token, refresh_token.
uncertainty: Whether the project still works against current Gemini CLI auth and Google ToS.
Code quality, security of credential handling, and recency of maintenance beyond README and file listing.
Accuracy of listed Gemini features (search grounding, thinking control) without inspecting source.
aiReview.tagline: Proxy Gemini CLI OAuth into OpenAI-style HTTP APIs
aiReview.description: Run a FastAPI proxy that maps Gemini CLI credentials to OpenAI-compatible chat and native Gemini generateContent endpoints with streaming.
pros: README documents OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions and native Gemini generateContent/stream endpoints.
Includes Docker, docker-compose, Hugging Face Spaces metadata, and a health check.
MIT license, public repo with Docker-oriented layout and environment-variable configuration.
Documents streaming, multimodal inputs, and optional search/thinking model suffixes.
cons: Positioned as a way to use Google’s free Gemini CLI quota through unofficial API surfaces, which may violate Google terms.
GitHub listing has no repository description or topics; README is the main documentation.
Requires injecting OAuth client secrets, tokens, and refresh tokens into the proxy environment.

aiReview.summary: Termux installer that runs a Gemini API reverse proxy (fork of geminicli2api) with OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Default auth is weak and a committed .env plus LAN sharing raise safety and ToS concerns for a developer directory.
evidence: README: 为 Android Termux 用户提供一键部署 Gemini API 反向代理服务; based on geminicli2api.
Auth section lists default密钥 123.
Repo listing includes .env, Setup.sh, run.py, FastAPI/Uvicorn in install steps.
175 stars, 24 forks, MIT, 28 commits.
uncertainty: Whether .env contains live secrets.
Whether proxy uses Google OAuth/CLI credentials vs user API keys.
Maintenance cadence beyond 28 commits.
aiReview.tagline: Termux one-click Gemini reverse-proxy installer
aiReview.description: Installs a FastAPI Gemini reverse proxy on Android Termux with a menu UI and OpenAI-compatible routes.
pros: Public MIT repo with README covering Termux install, menu management, and dual OpenAI/Gemini-style routes.
About 175 stars and 24 forks; 28 commits on main.
Explicitly based on gzzhongqi/geminicli2api rather than claiming original API client work.
cons: Ships a reverse proxy meant to reuse Gemini access and expose it on the LAN, which is a ToS and credential-sharing risk.
README documents a default key of 123 and the tree includes a committed .env.
GitHub About has no description; docs are marketing-heavy Chinese copy with a Bilibili/QQ funnel.

aiReview.summary: Open-source Gemini CLI wrapper that exposes Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash via an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions API. Useful for existing OpenAI clients, but it is a small fork with CORS * by default and optional Google-account OAuth for access.
evidence: GitHub description: Gemini CLI wrapper to serve Gemini models through an OpenAI-compatible API.
README feature table lists /v1/chat/completions, vision, tools, 1M-token context lift, CORS *.
LICENSE MIT; Docker and npm start on port 11434; AUTH_TYPE oauth-personal | gemini-api-key | vertex-ai.
uncertainty: Actual Gemini API vs unofficial CLI wrapping quality and rate-limit behavior not verified in code.
Last commit recency and production readiness of the TypeScript implementation not fully audited.
Compatibility claims with SillyTavern, LangChain, and Cline not independently tested.
aiReview.tagline: OpenAI-compatible HTTP API over Gemini CLI models
aiReview.description: Wraps Gemini CLI to serve chat completions, streaming, vision, and tools over an OpenAI-style local API.
pros: README documents OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with stream and non-stream modes.
Supports vision (image_url), function/tool calling, and reasoning thought chunks as stated in the feature table.
MIT-licensed TypeScript project with npm and Docker quick-start, env vars for PORT, AUTH_TYPE, GEMINI_API_KEY, and MODEL.
cons: Small project (about 13 commits, ~59 stars) forked from a Hugging Face original, so maintenance depth is limited.
CORS is enabled for all origins by default, which is a security concern if bound beyond localhost.
AUTH_TYPE oauth-personal is documented as using a Google account for Gemini 2.5 Pro access, which may conflict with intended API terms.

aiReview.summary: Open-source Cloudflare Worker that wraps Gemini CLI / Code Assist OAuth as an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API. Relevant for Gemini CLI users, but OAuth credential reuse and free-tier Code Assist routing warrant a human ToS/safety check.
evidence: GitHub description: Expose Gemini CLI endpoints as OpenAI API with Cloudflare Workers.
README features: OAuth2, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Cloudflare Workers, Code Assist free tier.
Repo stats on page: 895 stars, 205 forks, TypeScript, wrangler.toml, src/.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Exact LICENSE file and last commit date
Whether Code Assist OAuth proxying is allowed under Google terms
Production reliability of thinking/tool mapping
aiReview.tagline: OpenAI-compatible Gemini CLI proxy on Cloudflare Workers
aiReview.description: Deploy a Worker that maps OpenAI chat APIs to Gemini CLI OAuth, with streaming, tools, vision, and thinking controls.
pros: Public TypeScript Worker with README covering OAuth setup, models, streaming, tools, and vision.
About 895 stars, 205 forks, and 143 commits indicate active community interest.
Includes Docker, Wrangler config, HTTP test files, and examples.
Documents Gemini 2.5 models and thinking/reasoning_effort behavior.
cons: Setup copies Gemini CLI oauth_creds.json rather than using official Gemini API keys.
README highlights free-tier access via Code Assist, which may conflict with Google terms.
Last-commit recency and license were not fully verified in this pass.

aiReview.summary: Open-source FastAPI proxy that wraps Gemini CLI into an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions service. Useful for local prototyping, but it exists mainly to expose CLI-tier Gemini as an API and uses a dummy auth key, so ToS and safety review is warranted.
evidence: GitHub description and README: wrap Gemini CLI as OpenAI-compatible API for free Gemini 2.5 Pro.
Features: /v1/chat/completions, uvx, FastAPI + asyncio; default port 8765.
MIT license, tests directory, 152 stars, 24 forks, 20 commits.
Auth example uses Bearer dummy-key / any string.
uncertainty: Current Google ToS status of CLI-to-API wrapping.
Test coverage quality and last-commit recency beyond HTML snapshot.
Streaming, tool-calling, and production hardening not fully verified from truncated README.
aiReview.tagline: OpenAI-compatible HTTP wrapper around Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Run Gemini CLI as a local OpenAI-style chat completions API with FastAPI, uvx startup, and dummy Bearer auth.
pros: Implements an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint on FastAPI with documented curl and Python client examples.
MIT-licensed Python 3.12+ project with tests, pyproject/uv.lock, bilingual README, and ~20 commits.
Quick start via uvx and integration notes for Cherry Studio are documented.
cons: Positioned as a way to use free Gemini Pro/2.5 via API through the CLI, which may conflict with Google terms of use.
Default Authorization is a dummy key with no real authentication.
Small repo (152 stars, 20 commits) and depends on a separately installed, logged-in Gemini CLI.

aiReview.summary: Archived Node.js bridge that exposes Gemini CLI tools over MCP and an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API; docs are detailed but the repo is read-only as of Jul 2026.
evidence: GitHub page: Public archive, 138 stars, 29 forks, Apache-2.0, 17 commits.
README: MCP toolkit + OpenAI-compatible bridge built on google-gemini/gemini-cli.
README security warning: no user confirmation on tool invoke; default read-only; YOLO recommended only in containers.
npm badge for @intelligentinternet/gemini-cli-mcp-openai-bridge.
uncertainty: Whether the npm package still receives updates after archive.
Runtime quality, test coverage, and actual API compatibility were not executed.
Maintenance after Jul 2026 archive date.
aiReview.tagline: MCP and OpenAI-compatible bridge for Gemini CLI tools
aiReview.description: Expose Gemini CLI tools via MCP and an OpenAI-compatible chat API, with inherited auth and configurable security modes.
pros: Documents MCP exposure of gemini-cli tools and OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models endpoints.
Describes inherited gemini-cli authentication (cached login, GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS).
Documents security modes (read-only default, edit, configured, yolo) and warns that the bridge does not prompt for tool confirmation.
Apache-2.0 licensed with npm package, Dockerfile, and bilingual README.
cons: GitHub lists the repository as archived and read-only as of Jul 2, 2026.
GitHub About has no description; only 17 commits and a gemini-cli git submodule that can override a local install.
README clone/build URLs point at gemini-cli-common-bridge rather than this repo name.

aiReview.summary: Open-source Gemini CLI extension of slash-command prompt templates for coding, docs, testing, and debugging. Relevant to Gemini CLI users, but docs still use placeholder install paths and the repo has very few commits.
evidence: Repo description and README state it is a Gemini CLI Extension with slash commands.
About 411 stars and 108 forks on GitHub.
Features and command list documented in README.md.
uncertainty: Whether listed commands match files under commands/ and actually work in current Gemini CLI.
Last real update date and ongoing maintenance beyond three commits.
Exact license file presence beyond the MIT badge.
aiReview.tagline: Slash-command prompt templates for Gemini CLI tasks
aiReview.description: Install as a Gemini CLI extension to run curated slash commands for reviews, docs, tests, debugging, and architecture.
pros: Public GitHub repo packaged as a Gemini CLI extension with gemini-extension.json.
README lists 30+ categorized slash commands for common development tasks.
MIT license badge is shown on the repository.
cons: Installation examples still use placeholder paths like yourusername/prompt-library-extension.
History shows only three commits, a weak maintenance signal.
No API client or official Gemini SDK; prompts only.

aiReview.summary: Open-source MCP server that lets MCP clients (notably Claude) call Gemini CLI or the Antigravity (`agy`) CLI for large-context file and codebase analysis. Docs and npm packaging are solid, but the default backend is now experimental after Gemini CLI retirement for many users.
evidence: Repo description and README: MCP server wrapping Gemini CLI / agy for large token-window analysis.
Stars 2290, forks 213, TypeScript, npm package gemini-mcp-tool, docs at jamubc.github.io/gemini-mcp-tool.
README details GEMINI_MCP_BACKEND, AGY_CLI_PATH, GEMINI_MCP_TIMEOUT and Claude mcp add one-liner.
uncertainty: Could not verify live npm download counts, recent commit recency, or exact SPDX license vs MIT badge.
Could not independently verify Google Gemini CLI retirement date or Antigravity CLI behavior.
aiReview.tagline: MCP bridge to Gemini/Antigravity CLI for large-file analysis
aiReview.description: Expose Gemini or Antigravity CLI to MCP clients so assistants can analyze large files and codebases with @-path prompts.
pros: README documents MCP install (npx, Claude Desktop/Code), @-file prompts, sandbox usage, and backend env vars.
Repository includes TypeScript sources, tests, CI workflows, changelog, contributing guide, and VitePress docs.
Published on npm as gemini-mcp-tool with GitHub release badges and ~2.3k stars.
Supports switching between gemini and agy backends via GEMINI_MCP_BACKEND.
cons: Default backend after 2026-06-18 is experimental Antigravity CLI with Flash-only print mode and unsandboxed -p tool execution.
Depends on a separately installed Google CLI and auth; Gemini CLI is retired for several consumer tiers.
GitHub reports license as Other while the README badge says MIT.

aiReview.summary: Open-source MCP server that wraps Google’s Gemini CLI with googleSearch, chat, and analyzeFile tools. Useful for Claude/MCP clients; depends on Gemini CLI and exposes a yolo/sandbox flag that skips confirmations.
evidence: GitHub README: MCP wrapper for Gemini CLI with googleSearch, chat, analyzeFile.
Files: index.ts, tests/integration/tools.test.ts, package.json, bun.lock.
Stars 101, forks 16, language TypeScript, MIT stated in README.
uncertainty: Live npm download counts, CI status, and current Gemini CLI compatibility were not verified.
LICENSE file listed in README but not inspected in this pass.
aiReview.tagline: MCP server wrapping Gemini CLI search, chat, files
aiReview.description: Expose Gemini CLI as MCP tools for search, chat, and multimodal file analysis from compatible AI clients.
pros: README documents three MCP tools (googleSearch, chat, analyzeFile) and MCP client config including npx and Claude Code.
Repository includes TypeScript source, integration tests, lint/format config, and an MIT license notice.
Changelog records tool-name and package-name changes plus a Windows which-command fix.
Depends on official google-gemini/gemini-cli rather than reimplementing the Gemini API.
cons: Requires Gemini CLI (or --allow-npx) and Bun for local development.
Tools accept a yolo option that skips confirmations, which can increase unintended command risk.
Maintenance signals are modest (about 101 stars, 1 open issue) and last changelog date is 2025-07-03.

aiReview.summary: Small MIT-licensed Python MCP server that wraps the local Gemini CLI so Claude Code can call it for large-file analysis. Useful niche glue, but thin, Claude-oriented, and documents subprocess shell=True.
evidence: GitHub InfolabAI/gemini-cli-mcp: Python, MIT, 30 stars, files include gemini_mcp_server.py and test_gemini_mcp.py.
README describes wrapping gemini CLI via FastMCP and configuring ~/.claude.json.
Tool args are prompt, file_dir_url_path, and working_directory; command uses gemini -m gemini-2.5-flash.
uncertainty: Last commit recency and CI health not verified beyond the GitHub snapshot.
Whether Gemini CLI auth/quotas are handled beyond a local install.
Production hardening of path/prompt sanitization not reviewed in source.
aiReview.tagline: MCP wrapper that runs local Gemini CLI from Claude Code
aiReview.description: Expose local Gemini CLI as an MCP tool so Claude Code can analyze files, directories, or URLs via subprocess.
pros: MIT-licensed Python project with README, tests, and uv/pyproject setup.
Documents prerequisites, Claude Code MCP config, and a single run_gemini tool.
Targets Google Gemini CLI rather than inventing a separate API client.
cons: Primary audience is Claude Code token-saving, not first-party Gemini API apps.
README explicitly requires subprocess shell=True, which is a command-injection risk if prompts or paths are untrusted.
Small repo (~30 stars) with limited surface area and one open issue.

aiReview.summary: Small MIT TypeScript MCP server that exposes Gemini CLI to Claude Code via planning, analysis, and debug tools. Docs are clear but the repo is tiny, clone URLs are placeholders, and it is a community wrapper rather than an official Gemini SDK.
evidence: GitHub README: MCP server integrating Gemini AI with Claude Code; Node 18+, pnpm, Gemini CLI, Claude Code CLI.
Features: generate-plan, strategic-plan, review-approach, analyze-codebase, explain-concept, compare-technologies, gemini-consult, generate-tests, generate-docs, debug-assist.
License MIT; language TypeScript; src includes server.ts, gemini.ts, tools.ts, prompts.ts.
Stars 7, forks 1, issues 0 as of fetch.
uncertainty: Cannot verify code quality, secret handling, or last-commit recency beyond the README/file listing.
Cannot verify whether Gemini CLI usage is current or maintained.
No published package name or npm install path confirmed.
aiReview.tagline: MCP server that routes Claude Code to Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Run a TypeScript MCP server so Claude Code can call Gemini CLI for plans, analysis, tests, docs, and debugging.
pros: MIT TypeScript project with documented MCP tools that wrap Gemini CLI for Claude Code.
README lists prerequisites, build/start scripts, and how to register the server with claude mcp add.
Tools cover planning, codebase analysis, consult, tests, docs, and debug via generated Claude slash commands.
cons: Very small community project (7 stars, 1 fork) with no issues visible in the listing.
Install instructions still use a placeholder clone URL (yourusername/gemini-mcp).
Depends on separately installed Gemini CLI, Google AI credentials, and Claude Code rather than calling the Gemini API directly.

aiReview.summary: MIT TypeScript memory layer with a short Gemini CLI MCP setup doc; listed as a Gemini CLI guide but the repo is a general agent-memory product, not a Gemini API resource.
evidence: README describes a memory API (remember/recall/buildContext) and npm package goodmemory@0.8.3.
docs/GoodMemory-Gemini-CLI-Setup-Guide.md shows mcpServers.goodmemory with goodmemory-mcp --standalone.
GitHub metadata: MIT, TypeScript, 19 stars, 2 forks, CI and plugin-security-scan workflows present.
uncertainty: Cannot verify npm latest publish state or live Gemini CLI tool count (8/9) without running the CLI.
Maintenance cadence and security of MCP writeback in real Gemini CLI sessions not independently verified.
aiReview.tagline: Local SQLite memory layer with MCP for coding agents
aiReview.description: Add durable local memory to coding agents via MCP, including a Gemini CLI settings.json setup for read-only or opt-in write tools.
pros: Includes a dedicated Gemini CLI setup guide using ~/.gemini/settings.json and the goodmemory-mcp binary.
MIT-licensed TypeScript repo with CI workflows, ADRs, Python client, Docker, and extensive docs.
Documents local-first SQLite storage, MCP tools, and opt-in write via GOODMEMORY_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE.
cons: Canonical listing target is the whole GoodMemory product, not a Gemini API tutorial or SDK.
Primary hosts documented are Codex and Claude Code; Gemini CLI is a thin MCP configuration path.
Public benchmark claims for 0.8.3 are explicitly withheld as fail-closed.

aiReview.summary: Thin MIT Gemini CLI extension that installs a remote Mnemoverse MCP memory server with OAuth; relevant as a CLI add-on, not a first-party Gemini API SDK. Review for third-party hosted memory, OAuth scopes, and very low repo activity.
evidence: GitHub description: Gemini CLI extension with persistent Mnemoverse memory over MCP and OAuth.
Install command: gemini extensions install https://github.com/mnemoverse/gemini-extension.
Free-tier console mentioned; no credit card; scopes memory:read and memory:write.
Stars 2, forks 0, MIT License per GitHub API fetch.
uncertainty: Cannot verify MCP server security, data retention, or production reliability from this repo alone.
Actual gemini-extension.json contents and GEMINI.md quality not fully inspected beyond file list.
Free-tier limits and paid plans beyond README marketing links are unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Persistent shared agent memory via Gemini CLI MCP
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that connects OAuth MCP memory so agents can save and recall facts across tools.
pros: README documents gemini extensions install, OAuth 2.1 PKCE to mcp.mnemoverse.com, and GEMINI.md usage rules.
License is MIT; install manifest is a small GitHub repo wrapping a remote MCP connector.
Docs state memories are explicit tool writes only, with no delete tool on the connector.
Troubleshooting covers /extensions, /mcp, 401 refresh, and links to privacy policy.
cons: Repository has 2 stars, 0 forks, 0 issues, and only a few files (README, GEMINI.md, gemini-extension.json).
Runtime memory lives on a third-party remote server, not in this repo.
This is a Gemini CLI extension, not a Gemini Developer API client or official Google resource.

aiReview.summary: MIT Gemini CLI extension that registers a hosted Connections MCP server (events, contacts, Deal Flow, notes, payments) with browser OAuth; thin wrapper around a third-party SaaS, not a Gemini API SDK.
evidence: GitHub README: Connections for Gemini CLI, hosted MCP, nothing runs locally.
Install command targets gemini extensions install.
Pricing link: free base plan; Pass Pro from $39.99/mo.
Stars 1, forks 0, MIT license.
uncertainty: Cannot verify MCP server reliability, OAuth implementation, or data handling beyond README claims.
Maintenance cadence and real-world Gemini CLI compatibility are unverified.
aiReview.tagline: One-command Gemini CLI hookup to a hosted business MCP
aiReview.description: Installs a Gemini CLI extension that points at a hosted MCP server for events, contacts, deals, notes, and Stripe payments.
pros: README documents install via gemini extensions install and first-use browser OAuth.
Manifest is a small gemini-extension.json wrapping a remote streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint.
MIT license and community files are present.
cons: Repository has 1 star, 0 forks, and no issues; it is a thin wrapper with no local runtime.
Core product and data live on studio.connections.icu; Deal Flow posting requires a paid plan.
Not a Gemini API client or tutorial; relevance is Gemini CLI extension plumbing only.

aiReview.summary: Neovim plugin that embeds Gemini CLI (plus Qwen and Claude Code) via MCP/sidebar, diffs, and tmux. Directly useful for Gemini CLI users in Neovim; quality looks solid but it is a third-party editor companion, not an official SDK.
evidence: README states MCP-backed Neovim companion inspired by vscode-gemini-companion.
Prerequisites list google-gemini/gemini-cli plus qwen-code and claude-code.
Code layout includes lua/gemini, tests, and .github/workflows/tests.yml.
uncertainty: License file contents and security of WebSocket/auth for Claude were not independently audited.
Recent commit cadence and issue resolution quality not verified beyond GitHub snapshot.
aiReview.tagline: Neovim MCP sidecar for Gemini CLI and other agents
aiReview.description: Embed Gemini CLI in Neovim with MCP context, diffs, diagnostics, and optional Qwen/Claude sessions without leaving the editor.
pros: Integrates official gemini-cli via PATH auto-detect, MCP-style IDE context, diffs, and Neovim commands.
README documents install, commands, sidebar presets, tmux, and tests using PlenaryBusted.
Repository includes Lua source, GitHub Actions tests, and a modest but active star/fork count.
cons: Also wraps Qwen and Claude Code, so it is not Gemini-API-only.
Requires separate CLI installs and plenary.nvim; Claude path uses WebSocket MCP and lock files.
Community plugin (84 stars, 2 issues); long-term maintenance is not guaranteed.

aiReview.summary: Neovim plugin that opens Gemini CLI in a split, checks/installs the CLI, and can send visual selections. Small Lua project with basic docs; useful for Neovim users already on Gemini CLI, not a Gemini API SDK.
evidence: GitHub README: Neovim plugin to integrate Gemini CLI; Neovim >= 0.7.0; Node.js/npm required.
Keymaps documented: <leader>og toggle, <leader>sg send visual selection.
Repo stats from GitHub fetch: 57 stars, 8 forks, 1 issue, language Lua.
uncertainty: License file not shown in the file list snippet.
Code quality, install-prompt safety, and last-commit recency not independently audited beyond README.
Behavior of CLI install prompt and terminal job handling not verified by running the plugin.
aiReview.tagline: Neovim split for Gemini CLI with selection send
aiReview.description: Open Gemini CLI in a Neovim split, set EDITOR to nvim, and send visual selections via keymaps after optional CLI install checks.
pros: README documents lazy.nvim, packer, and vim-plug install plus split_direction setup.
Features include toggle split, gemini CLI presence check/install prompt, EDITOR=nvim, and visual-mode send keymap.
Repository is Lua with a small, inspectable plugin layout (lua/gemini, plugin/gemini.vim).
Listed in Awesome Gemini CLI with 57 stars at review time.
cons: Depends on an external gemini CLI and Node/npm rather than calling the Gemini API directly.
Docs are short: one keymap pair, one config option, and no license/maintenance details in the fetched README.
Only 57 stars, 8 forks, and 1 issue; longevity and review depth are limited.

aiReview.summary: Unofficial Neovim plugin that embeds the Google Gemini CLI (or Claude Code) in a persistent terminal window. Thin wrapper around the CLI, not the Gemini API; small repo with limited maintenance signals.
evidence: README: unofficial plugin to run gemini/claude in a persistent Neovim terminal.
Requirements: Neovim >= 0.8, Gemini CLI >= 0.1.19 or Claude Code, Node.js >= 22.
Repo metadata: Lua, 6 stars, 2 forks, 1 issue; lua/gemini-nvim/init.lua plus agents-parter modules.
uncertainty: License, commit recency, and runtime safety of companion packages were not verified.
Whether gemini-nvim is a stable public plugin vs a monorepo alias is unclear.
aiReview.tagline: Run Gemini CLI in a persistent Neovim terminal
aiReview.description: Embed Google Gemini CLI or Claude Code in Neovim with a toggleable float or side terminal and checkhealth.
pros: README documents setup, window styles, agent list, keymaps, and :Gemini usage.
Supports Neovim :checkhealth for gemini executable and Node.js.
Configurable to launch the Gemini CLI with extra params and env vars.
cons: GitHub listing is JunYang-tes/agents-parter.nvim, not a dedicated gemini-nvim package, with only 6 stars.
Install notes mix neovim-ide-companion and neovim-gemini-companion and recommend global bun/npm installs.
Depends on a separately installed Gemini CLI rather than calling the Gemini API directly.

aiReview.summary: TypeScript CLI that adapts SPARC multi-agent orchestration for Gemini CLI; community-maintained with npm packaging, but the author flags immaturity and limited tests.
evidence: Repo README: adaptation of ruvnet/claude-code-flow for Gemini CLI; features list SPARC, up to 10 agents, memory, multimodal.
Stars 158, forks 21, TypeScript, npm gemini-code-flow.
File tree includes src/cli.ts, orchestrator, gemini-client, path-security, rate-limiter; tests/example.test.ts and a few util tests.
uncertainty: Actual runtime quality and Gemini API usage vs wrapping the Gemini CLI only.
License file contents vs GitHub 'Other'.
Maintenance beyond listed issues and last activity.
aiReview.tagline: SPARC multi-agent orchestration on top of Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Run SPARC modes and parallel Gemini CLI agents with shared memory, multimodal inputs, and Google-account or API-key auth.
pros: Targets Gemini CLI with SPARC modes, parallel agents, and persistent memory as documented in the README.
Published as a global npm package with TypeScript sources, GitHub issue templates, and a publish workflow.
Documents Google-account and GEMINI_API_KEY auth plus rate-limit caveats.
cons: README and contributing notes describe the project as an early adaptation needing reviews, tests, and architecture help.
GitHub reports license as Other while README claims MIT.
Automated tests appear sparse relative to the CLI surface.

aiReview.summary: Proof-of-concept Gemini CLI custom commands and extensions that orchestrate prompt-driven sub-agents via filesystem state. Useful as a learning demo, but it is not production-ready and relies on the --yolo flag.
evidence: GitHub README: Prompt-Driven Sub-Agent Orchestrator with /agents:start|run|status|type.
Repo files include .gemini/commands/*.toml and extensions (coder-agent, reviewer-agent, tdd-agent).
Disclaimer: not secure for production; relies on --yolo.
91 stars, 26 forks, 3 issues; language listed as Shell.
uncertainty: License file was not confirmed from the fetched listing.
Recent commit activity and issue health were not verified beyond the README snapshot.
Whether the demo still works against current Gemini CLI versions was not tested.
aiReview.tagline: Filesystem-state sub-agent orchestration via CLI commands
aiReview.description: Demo of prompt-defined CLI commands that queue, run, and track specialized sub-agents using directories as state.
pros: README documents architecture, directory layout, commands, and an end-to-end workflow.
Includes .toml custom commands, agent extensions, and example personas under .gemini/.
Explicitly points to official CLI docs, a related roadmap issue, and a security disclaimer.
cons: Stated as a proof-of-concept, not a maintained production system.
Uses the -y/--yolo flag and is described as not secure for production.
Agent logic lives in prompts rather than tested application code.

aiReview.summary: Community guide of ~30 tips for Google’s Gemini CLI covering setup, GEMINI.md context, MCP, scripting, and safety features. Strong learning resource for agentic terminal workflows; not an SDK or official product.
evidence: Repo description: Gemini CLI Tips and Tricks; README title Gemini CLI Tips & Tricks covering ~30 pro-tips.
Install examples: npm install -g @google/gemini-cli and npx @google/gemini-cli.
GitHub stats from page: 2.4k stars, 105 forks, 28 commits on main, README-only file tree.
Topics: gemini, gemini-api, gemini-cli; author addyosmani.
uncertainty: Exact last-commit date and license file not confirmed from the HTML snapshot.
Accuracy of every CLI flag versus current @google/gemini-cli release not verified.
Whether README is kept in sync with Google’s official docs.
aiReview.tagline: Pro tips for agentic coding in the Gemini terminal
aiReview.description: Covers setup, persistent context, custom commands, MCP, checkpointing, headless mode, and IDE integration for terminal-based Gemini workflows.
pros: Public GitHub repo with a long structured README of numbered Gemini CLI tips.
Covers install, auth (Google login vs GEMINI_API_KEY), slash commands, GEMINI.md, MCP, YOLO mode caution, and GitHub Action usage.
About 2.4k stars, 105 forks, 28 commits, and topics including gemini-cli and gemini-api.
Maintained by a well-known author and listed in awesome-gemini-cli.
cons: Documentation-only repo (README); no code library to pin or version as an SDK.
Some setup details cite third-party cheatsheets and may drift from upstream CLI changes.
Includes YOLO auto-approve and shell-passthrough advice that can be unsafe if followed blindly.

aiReview.summary: Personal collection of Google Gemini CLI commands, extensions, and settings with Apache-2.0 docs and install scripts that copy `.gemini` files. Content is thin (few commits, mostly documentation of official CLI features) and the clone/rsync install can overwrite existing configs.
evidence: GitHub description: Collection of helpful gemini cli extensions and commands.
README titled personal extensions/commands/settings for google-gemini/gemini-cli; Apache-2.0 license; ~147 stars, 7 forks.
Install commands rsync cloned `.gemini/` into ~/.gemini or ./.gemini with an overwrite note.
uncertainty: Exact set of shipped custom commands beyond the listed .gemini/commands/plan path was not fully enumerated.
Last-commit recency and ongoing maintenance beyond six commits were not independently verified.
Whether the collection is still aligned with current Gemini CLI extension APIs is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Personal Gemini CLI commands, extensions, and settings
aiReview.description: Install personal Gemini CLI commands, extensions, and settings via clone and rsync into global or project `.gemini` directories.
pros: Public Apache-2.0 repo documenting Gemini CLI custom commands, extensions, settings, and GEMINI.md context.
Includes example TOML command and gemini-extension.json patterns plus links to official CLI docs.
Install snippets cover both global (~/.gemini) and project-local copies.
cons: Repository history is very small (about six commits) and the tree is mostly README plus a commands path.
Install uses git clone plus rsync and may overwrite existing configuration files with the same name.
Much of the README restates official Gemini CLI documentation rather than shipping a large unique command set.

aiReview.summary: Small Apache-2.0 Gemini CLI extension that wires official Gemini API llms.txt docs via an mcpdoc MCP server plus GEMINI.md context. Thin config wrapper with only four commits, so treat as a convenience starter rather than a maintained product.
evidence: GitHub about: Gemini CLI extension that adds Gemini API docs and MCP.
README clones into Gemini CLI extensions dirs and auto-loads.
gemini-extension.json uses uvx mcpdoc with GeminiApiDocs and GeminiApiReference llms.txt URLs.
Apache-2.0; 4 commits on main.
uncertainty: Author affiliation with Google/Gemini not verified from the page.
mcpdoc package security and maintenance not reviewed.
Whether the extension still matches current Gemini CLI extension schema.
aiReview.tagline: CLI extension for official Gemini API docs via MCP
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that loads Gemini API docs and reference via mcpdoc MCP and system instructions.
pros: Targets Gemini CLI with install paths under ~/.gemini/extensions or workspace .gemini/extensions.
Points MCP at official ai.google.dev Gemini API docs and API reference llms.txt URLs.
Apache-2.0 license with README install steps and a reusable mcpServers snippet.
Includes GEMINI.md plus CoC, contributing, and security policy files.
cons: Repository has only four commits and modest community signals (about 55 stars, 8 forks).
Functionality depends on uvx and the third-party mcpdoc package rather than first-party Gemini SDK code.
No releases or substantial implementation beyond config and markdown.

aiReview.summary: Experimental Gemini CLI example that wires Vertex MCP Genmedia (Imagen 4, Veo 3) and gemini-2.5-flash-image for iterative image/video generation. Useful as a setup walkthrough, but it is a small, vibe-coded demo (few commits, incomplete demo video) and not production-ready.
evidence: GitHub description and README: example of Gemini CLI with MCP Servers for Genmedia and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image.
Topics include gemini-cli, imagen, veo3, mcp-server, video-generation.
NOTE section: demonstration of vibe coding; not intended for production.
License Apache-2.0; 19 stars, 6 forks, 4 commits on main.
uncertainty: Cannot verify last-commit recency or code quality beyond README and file tree.
MCP sample settings and Vertex Creative Studio dependency health not independently tested.
Ongoing maintenance and Vertex API cost/quotas not documented in detail.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI MCP demo for Imagen, Veo, and image edits
aiReview.description: Shows Gemini CLI plus Vertex Genmedia MCP servers to ideate, generate, and edit images and videos with Imagen 4, Veo 3, and Flash Image.
pros: README documents Vertex AI, gcloud, Gemini CLI, MCP Genmedia, GCS bucket, and settings.sample.json setup steps.
Targets Imagen 4, Veo 3, and gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview for character/scene-consistent edits.
Apache-2.0 license with example prompts, generated media folders, and GEMINI.md for CLI context.
cons: Author states it is a vibe-coded demonstration, not for production, and all assets/code are AI-generated.
Only four commits, 19 stars, and the demo video link is still TODO.
Setup clones another Google Cloud repo and requires Vertex APIs, IAM, and a storage bucket.

aiReview.summary: Community demo collection for Google’s Gemini CLI covering agents, Workspace, SQLite, and git workflows. Useful for learning and workshops, not a production library; several demos are incomplete.
evidence: GitHub description: Demos-in-a-box for Gemini CLI.
Demo table includes adk-with-skills (Agents), auto-slide-creator, sqlite-investigation, google-sheets-mcp.
Note: intended for demonstration purposes only.
318 commits, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING.md present.
uncertainty: License SPDX not confirmed from LICENSE file text.
Last commit date and CI health not verified beyond README CI/CD notes.
Demo completeness and test coverage not inspected in each folder.
aiReview.tagline: Boxed Gemini CLI demos for agents, data, and Workspace
aiReview.description: Open-source demo folders showing Gemini CLI on agents, Sheets, SQLite, and git, with GEMINI.md scripts and workshop notes.
pros: README lists multiple Gemini CLI demos with status, category, and short descriptions.
Repo includes LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, GEMINI.md, justfile, and 300+ commits.
Contributing asks each demo for GEMINI.md, SCRIPT.md, README.md, purpose, repeatable code, and tests.
Install points at npx @gemini/gemini-cli and the official google-gemini/gemini-cli repo.
cons: README states the project is demonstration-only and not for production.
Several listed demos are marked WIP or incomplete.
Star count is low (14) relative to forks, so popularity and quality signals are mixed.

aiReview.summary: Curated GitHub awesome-list of tools, extensions, forks, and docs for Gemini CLI, with 500+ stars and active commits. Useful discovery resource, not an implementation of the Gemini API itself.
evidence: GitHub description: curated list of tools, extensions, and resources for Gemini CLI.
Topics include gemini, gemini-api, gemini-cli, awesome-list.
About 522 stars, 205 forks, 334 commits, CC0-1.0, CONTRIBUTING.md present.
Official section links google-gemini/gemini-cli, cookbook, and run-gemini-cli GitHub Action.
uncertainty: Link freshness and whether listed third-party projects remain maintained or safe.
Exact last-commit date not extracted from HTML snapshot.
aiReview.tagline: Curated tools and extensions for the Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Lists official and community tools, forks, UIs, MCP servers, and docs for Google’s Gemini CLI agent.
pros: Public CC0-licensed awesome-list focused on Gemini CLI with official links to google-gemini/gemini-cli and related Google resources.
Organized sections cover official tools, interfaces, forks, orchestration, SDKs, MCP servers, and documentation.
Repository shows substantial activity (hundreds of commits, 500+ stars, contributing guide).
Points to the official Gemini CLI cookbook and GitHub Action for CI.
cons: It is a link directory, not an SDK, API client, or runnable product.
Many entries are third-party GUIs, forks, and commercial apps whose quality and safety vary.
README leads with vendor product promotion (Piebald) before the list.

aiReview.summary: Official-looking Gemini CLI extension that generates and edits images via Nano Banana (Gemini image) models over MCP, with slash commands and Apache-2.0 licensing. Docs and stars are strong, but GitHub has no About blurb and image-preview models imply API cost and preview-model churn.
evidence: README: Nano Banana Gemini CLI extension; default gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview; NANOBANANA_API_KEY and NANOBANANA_MODEL.
Install via gemini extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/nanobanana.
Repo files: gemini-extension.json, mcp-server, commands, Apache-2.0, SECURITY.md.
Stars ~1.1k, forks ~130, 23 commits.
uncertainty: Whether gemini-cli-extensions org is Google-official.
Runtime quality of MCP image pipelines and prompt-injection handling.
Stability of preview model IDs over time.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension for image gen, edit, and restore
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that generates, edits, and restores images via Gemini image models and slash commands.
pros: Provides Gemini CLI slash commands for generate, edit, restore, icons, patterns, stories, and diagrams.
Uses an MCP server with TypeScript modules for Gemini API calls and file handling.
Documents model selection, Node 20+, API key from Google AI Studio, and gemini extensions install.
Apache-2.0 license, SECURITY.md, contributing notes, changelog, and CI workflow are present.
Public repo with about 1.1k stars and 130 forks.
cons: GitHub About has no description, website, or topics.
Depends on preview image models and a paid Gemini API key.
Only 23 commits on main, so long-term maintenance is not deeply evidenced.

aiReview.summary: Tiny Gemini CLI extension that points MCP at a local Blender HTTP server; README is one line and the manifest sets trust:true, so treat as a thin glue snippet rather than a maintained product.
evidence: Repo description and README: A super simple extension to enable Blender via MCP for Gemini CLI.
gemini-extension.json name blender-mcp version 0.1.0 with httpUrl http://localhost:9876 and trust true.
GitHub shows MIT license, 5 commits, 10 stars, 4 forks.
uncertainty: Whether a Blender MCP process must already be running on port 9876.
Last-commit recency and ongoing maintenance beyond five commits.
Runtime safety of trusting the local MCP server.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI MCP hook for local Blender
aiReview.description: Connect Gemini CLI to Blender over a local MCP HTTP endpoint with a minimal extension manifest.
pros: Targets Gemini CLI via gemini-extension.json and an MCP server named blender.
MIT-licensed public GitHub repository.
Manifest is small and easy to inspect.
cons: README is a single sentence with no install, Blender, or MCP setup steps.
Only five commits, ~10 stars, and no documented tests or changelog.
mcpServers.blender sets trust: true against http://localhost:9876 with no auth notes.

aiReview.summary: Open-source Gemini CLI extension that captures webcam frames via MCP/OpenCV and chains them into Gemini image, Veo video, and ASL modes. Relevant for CLI multimodal work; camera access and API keys warrant normal privacy caution.
evidence: GitHub description: webcam access, single-frame capture, and ASL modes for Gemini-CLI.
README documents gemini extensions install, /vision:devices/start/capture/banana/veo/asl, and MCP/OpenCV.
LICENSE listed as Apache-2.0; safety notes on consent and /vision:stop.
uncertainty: Runtime reliability of camera backends and ASL transcription not independently tested.
Last-commit freshness and issue/maintenance cadence not fully verified.
Whether Veo billing/quotas are fully documented beyond env keys.
aiReview.tagline: Webcam capture, ASL, and Veo from Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Add webcam capture, ASL interpretation, Gemini image styling, and Veo video generation to Gemini CLI via slash commands.
pros: Installs as a Gemini CLI extension with documented /vision:* slash commands.
Uses FastMCP, OpenCV, Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, and Veo 3 as described in the README.
Apache-2.0 license with install instructions, architecture notes, and a safety section.
Public repo with 51 stars, 6 forks, and 38 commits on main.
cons: Requires local camera permission plus GEMINI_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY for Veo.
macOS-oriented permission notes; Windows/Linux camera support is not clearly specified.
ASL and Veo quality cannot be verified from docs alone.

aiReview.summary: Small Apache-2.0 Gemini CLI extension for voice input and audio output; README is one install command and notes an OpenAI TTS dependency. Thin docs and low activity make it a review, not a strong directory pick.
evidence: GitHub description: voice input and audio output; requires OpenAI for TTS.
Install documented as gemini extensions install of the git URL.
About 5 stars, 3 forks, 8 commits on main.
Listed as Talk in awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
uncertainty: Code quality, MCP/server behavior, and how OpenAI keys are handled were not audited.
Whether voice I/O works across platforms is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Voice in and audio out for Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that adds voice input and spoken output, currently using OpenAI for TTS.
pros: Targets Gemini CLI via gemini extensions install and gemini-extension.json.
Apache-2.0 license is present on the repository.
Stated purpose is voice input and audio output for the CLI.
cons: README has almost no usage, setup, or API documentation beyond a single install command.
TTS currently depends on OpenAI rather than Gemini-native audio.
Repository shows few stars, forks, and commits, so maintenance is hard to judge.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that exposes Computer Use / browser MCP tools (headful browsing, JS execution, scrolling). Relevant for CLI users, but computer-control surface and community maintenance warrant a closer look.
evidence: GitHub description: A Google Gemini-CLI extension than enables Gemini Computer Use from the CLI.
Install command: gemini extensions install https://github.com/automateyournetwork/GeminiCLI_ComputerUse_Extension.git.
README examples call initialize_browser, execute_action (scroll, JS), capture_state, and headless=false.
Apache-2.0 license; ~32 commits, 91 stars, 22 forks as of page fetch.
uncertainty: Last-commit recency and ongoing maintenance quality.
Whether Computer Use tools are sandboxed or require extra API/model access.
Exact MCP server implementation safety (credentials, origin restrictions).
aiReview.tagline: CLI extension for Gemini Computer Use browser control
aiReview.description: Installs Gemini CLI Computer Use tools to drive a browser, capture state, and run visible browsing workflows from prompts.
pros: Public GitHub repo with Apache-2.0 license, README, gemini-extension.json, and install via gemini extensions install.
Documents Gemini CLI Computer Use MCP flows including initialize_browser, execute_action, and capture_state.
Modest community signal (about 91 stars, 22 forks) and listed in awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
cons: Enables headful browser control, JavaScript execution, and scrolling, which is a high-privilege agent surface.
README is long example-prompt oriented rather than a full API/security/limitations guide.
Maintenance depth (tests, release cadence, dependency review) is not established from the listing alone.

aiReview.summary: Official Figma Gemini CLI extension repo is archived and deprecated; maintainers redirect users to the MCP server guide. Do not list this URL as an active Gemini CLI extension.
evidence: GitHub banner: This repository was archived by the owner on Mar 26, 2026.
README title: DEPRECATED Gemini CLI Extension; About link is github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide.
Public archive, Apache-2.0, 124 stars, 10 forks, 8 commits.
uncertainty: Successor mcp-server-guide quality and Gemini CLI compatibility were not reviewed.
Exact original extension capabilities are not documented beyond deprecation notes.
aiReview.tagline: Archived Figma Gemini CLI extension, now MCP-based
aiReview.description: Deprecated Gemini CLI extension for Figma; functionality moved to an MCP implementation. Use the successor repo instead.
pros: Published under the official Figma GitHub org with an Apache-2.0 license.
README clearly marks the project deprecated and points to github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide.
Was a Gemini CLI extension, so it matches the directory topic historically.
cons: Repository was archived on Mar 26, 2026 and is read-only.
Only 8 commits and essentially README plus a leftover gemini-extension-old.json; no maintained extension code.
Maintainers state no further security patches or feature updates will be pushed.

aiReview.summary: Archived Gemini CLI extension that searches Google Fonts and Material Icons via local tools; relevant to Gemini CLI but unmaintained (archived Oct 2025) with low community traction.
evidence: GitHub description and README: Gemini CLI extension for Google Fonts + Material Icons and Symbols.
Banner: archived by the owner on Oct 27, 2025.
Install command: gemini extension install https://github.com/rodydavis/google-fonts-gemini-cli-extension.
Tools listed: search_fonts, search_icons, search_font_tags, get_icon_categories, get_icon_styles.
Apache-2.0 license; 24 commits; 13 stars; 0 forks.
uncertainty: Whether the local google_fonts.sqlite data is current.
Runtime behavior and safety of scripts/MCP-style tools were not executed.
Replacement or successor after archival is unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Search Google Fonts and Material Icons from Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install as a Gemini CLI extension to search fonts, tags, and Material Icons from a local SQLite catalog without leaving the terminal.
pros: Documents Gemini CLI install and five search tools for fonts, tags, and icons.
Apache-2.0 license with tests, TypeScript, and gemini-extension.json.
Uses a local SQLite catalog rather than requiring a live Google Fonts API key.
cons: Repository was archived on Oct 27, 2025 and is read-only.
Only 13 stars, 0 forks, and Node.js v24+ is required.
Clone instructions in the README still mention a mismatched directory name.

aiReview.summary: Official-looking Gemini CLI extension that proxies GitLab’s hosted MCP API for issues, MRs, pipelines, and search. Docs are usable but the repo is young (few commits), SaaS feature flags are required, and the install/distribution examples disagree.
evidence: README: GitLab MCP Extension for Gemini CLI targeting https://gitlab.com/api/v4/mcp.
Install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/GitLab-Ecosystem/Gemini-CLI-Extensions.
License Apache 2.0; commands/*.toml listed; npm test mentioned.
uncertainty: Whether GitLab-Ecosystem is an official GitLab org vs community.
Current enablement of required SaaS feature flags.
Which install URL (this repo vs benvenker/gitlab-gemini-extension) is canonical.
aiReview.tagline: MCP bridge from Gemini CLI to hosted DevOps APIs
aiReview.description: Installs a Gemini CLI extension that talks to a hosted MCP server for issues, merge requests, pipelines, notes, and search.
pros: README documents gemini extensions install, Node 20+, Gemini CLI v0.8.0+, and OAuth first-run.
Commands map to MCP tools for issues, MRs, pipelines, notes, and search.
Apache 2.0 with tests, TypeScript build, and gemini-extension.json at the repo root.
cons: Only 15 stars, 3 forks, and 5 commits, so maintenance is still thin.
Requires GitLab SaaS mcp_server and oauth_dynamic_client_generation flags.
Distribution section cites a different GitHub path than the install command.

aiReview.summary: Open-source Gemini CLI extension that connects a local Obsidian vault with RAG (LanceDB), graph/link tools, and note management. Directly relevant and well documented; extra npm install and heavy first-time indexing are real setup costs.
evidence: GitHub description: Gemini CLI extension for Obsidian with local-first RAG.
README lists RAG, graph traversal, link repair, journaling, and management tools.
gemini-extension.json present; install via gemini extensions install.
ISC license, tests (vitest), docs/demo.gif, SECURITY.md.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions as Obsidian.
uncertainty: Exact last-commit recency and CI pass status not verified from API.
Embedding model/provider used for indexing not fully specified in the excerpt.
Runtime safety of vault write tools not independently audited.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension for local Obsidian vault RAG
aiReview.description: Connect Gemini CLI to a local Obsidian vault with semantic search, wikilink graph tools, journaling, and note CRUD.
pros: Installs as a Gemini CLI extension and exposes MCP tools plus slash commands such as /obsidian:ask and /obsidian:index.
Local-first RAG uses LanceDB with a vector index stored under ~/.gemini-obsidian-lancedb.
README documents vault configuration, native dependency install, indexing tuning, tests, and an ISC license.
Repository includes src, tests, changelog, contributing, and security policy files.
About 102 stars, 11 forks, and 89 commits indicate active community interest.
cons: Semantic search requires a second npm install in the extension directory for native LanceDB binaries.
First-time indexing can take many minutes and high CPU on large vaults.
Tools always use a single configured vault path, not a per-call vault argument.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that installs an MCP server to search and install skills, prompts, MCP configs, and workflows from the TokRepo registry. Thin repo (one commit, no stars) with a short README and MIT license; treat as a small third-party CLI add-on, not a first-party Gemini API SDK.
evidence: GitHub description: TokRepo extension for Gemini CLI to search installable AI assets.
Install command: gemini extension install https://github.com/henu-wang/tokrepo-gemini-extension.
MCP config uses npx tokrepo-mcp-server; MIT license listed on the repo page.
uncertainty: Runtime quality and security of tokrepo-mcp-server and registry assets were not audited.
Whether TokRepo registry content is moderated or paid is unknown.
Commit recency and GEMINI.md contents were not fully inspected beyond the GitHub landing page.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension to search and install AI assets
aiReview.description: Installs a TokRepo MCP server in Gemini CLI so you can search, inspect, and install skills, prompts, MCP configs, and workflows.
pros: README documents gemini extension install and MCP tools tokrepo_search, tokrepo_detail, tokrepo_install, and tokrepo_trending.
MIT-licensed public GitHub repo with gemini-extension.json and GEMINI.md.
Points to npm packages tokrepo-mcp-server and tokrepo plus tokrepo.com as the registry.
cons: Repository shows 0 stars, 0 forks, and a single commit, so maintenance is unproven.
Does not implement the Gemini Developer API; it only wires Gemini CLI to a third-party MCP/registry.
Installing via npx tokrepo-mcp-server implies running unvetted third-party installable assets.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that routes document extraction, PII redaction, and contract review through the paid ParseRail API via MCP. Small, early repo with clear install docs; requires a paid key and has almost no community traction.
evidence: GitHub description and README: Gemini CLI extension using parserail-mcp.
Install command: gemini extensions install https://github.com/kyisaiah47/parserail-gemini-extension.
README states no free tier and pay-per-successful-call billing.
~22 commits, 1 star, 0 forks on a public repo.
uncertainty: Whether all ~38 tools work as advertised in Gemini CLI.
Ongoing maintenance and security of the MCP server and key handling.
Exact credit rates and SLA of the commercial ParseRail API.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI tools for invoices, PII redaction, contracts
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that calls ParseRail MCP tools for financial docs, redaction, and contract review.
pros: README documents Gemini CLI install, API key prompt, Node 18+, and example prompts.
Targets document extraction, PII redaction, and contract review via an MCP server package.
Includes gemini-extension.json and GEMINI.md for tool routing.
cons: ParseRail has no free tier; keys and credit packs start around $19–$20.
Repository shows 1 star, 0 forks, and limited independent verification of tool quality.
Canonical listing URL used a different repo name than the live GitHub path.

aiReview.summary: Official open-source Gemini CLI extension that adds /code-review and /pr-code-review commands to analyze local branch or GitHub PR diffs. Requires Gemini CLI ≥0.4.0; PR review needs the GitHub MCP server and env or a PR URL.
evidence: GitHub description: Google's Code Review extension for the Gemini CLI that reviews your code changes.
README install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/code-review; requires Gemini CLI v0.4.0+.
Commands documented: /code-review for current branch; /pr-code-review with PR link or env vars.
License Apache-2.0; topics gemini, gemini-cli, gemini-cli-extensions; ~532 stars, 41 forks.
Authors tied to Gemini Code Assist GitHub App in README.
uncertainty: Cannot verify ongoing maintenance cadence, test coverage, or issue backlog from the listing page alone.
Runtime behavior and false-positive rates of the review commands were not executed.
gemini-cli is not in the allowed tag list.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI commands to review local and PR diffs
aiReview.description: Adds Gemini CLI commands that analyze branch and GitHub pull-request changes for code quality issues.
pros: Published under gemini-cli-extensions as Google’s Code Review extension for Gemini CLI.
README documents install via gemini extensions install, CLI version requirement, and /code-review plus /pr-code-review usage.
Apache-2.0 license with contributing, code of conduct, and links to Gemini CLI extension docs.
Public repo with hundreds of stars and tens of forks.
PR flow documents GitHub MCP enablement and REPOSITORY, PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER, and ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT.
cons: History is short (about 12 commits) and there are no GitHub Releases listed on the repo page.
Pull-request reviews depend on extra GitHub MCP setup rather than working out of the box.
Quality of reviews is not independently evidenced beyond the README and GitHub App attribution.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Gemini CLI extension that adds /security:analyze and /security:scan-deps to review diffs/PRs and check dependencies via OSV-Scanner. Apache-2.0, well documented, with a note that reports are first-pass analysis only.
evidence: Repo description: Google's Security extension for Gemini CLI that finds vulnerabilities in code changes and PRs.
README: gemini extensions install; /security:analyze; /security:scan-deps with OSV-Scanner.
~795 stars, 59 forks, Apache-2.0, SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md present.
uncertainty: False-positive/false-negative rates of the AI security report are not independently verified.
Exact last-commit recency beyond 218 commits on main was not timestamped in this review.
aiReview.tagline: CLI extension that scans diffs and deps for vulnerabilities
aiReview.description: Adds Gemini CLI commands to analyze code changes and pull requests plus OSV-based dependency scans.
pros: Google-maintained Gemini CLI extension with Apache-2.0 license and 218 commits.
Documents /security:analyze for branch diffs and /security:scan-deps using OSV-Scanner.
Includes GitHub workflow integration, contributing, changelog, and security policy.
README states analysis is a first-pass report, not a full audit.
cons: Non-interactive /security:analyze is not supported yet (issue #20).
Effectiveness depends on Gemini CLI v0.4.0+ and git/GitHub setup.

aiReview.summary: Official-looking Gemini CLI extension that delegates coding work to Google’s Jules background agent via /jules. Apache-2.0 repo with install docs; Jules account and GitHub connection are required, and CLI install may prompt for sudo.
evidence: GitHub description and README: Gemini CLI extension to orchestrate Jules for coding tasks.
Install command requires Gemini CLI v0.4.0+; topics include gemini, gemini-cli, gemini-cli-extensions.
License Apache-2.0; links to jules.google and Gemini CLI extensions docs.
uncertainty: Jules backend pricing and availability not verified from this repo.
Code quality of mcp-server and commands not reviewed beyond README listing.
Release cadence and last-commit date not fully extracted from the HTML snapshot.
aiReview.tagline: Delegate coding tasks to a background agent from CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that offloads bug fixes, refactors, and dependency updates to an asynchronous coding agent.
pros: README documents install via gemini extensions, /jules usage, and prerequisites (Jules account plus GitHub repo connection).
Repository is Apache-2.0 with CONTRIBUTING.md, gemini-extension.json, commands, and an mcp-server directory.
Public GitHub stats show 413 stars and 51 forks under gemini-cli-extensions.
Stated use cases include bug fixing, refactoring, dependency updates, and documentation maintenance with branch submission.
cons: Only 14 commits on main, so long-term maintenance depth is limited to observe.
Depends on an external Jules account and connected GitHub repository, not the Gemini API alone.
README notes Gemini CLI may run npm install with sudo, which is a privilege-elevation concern.

aiReview.summary: Official experimental Gemini CLI extension that adds Flutter/Dart project bootstrap, modification, and commit workflows. Directly relevant to Gemini CLI users, with clear install docs and BSD-3-Clause licensing.
evidence: https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/flutter README: Flutter extension for Gemini CLI; experimental; gemini extensions install from this repo.
License file linked as BSD-3-Clause; 401 stars, 27 forks, 75 commits.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions curated README as flutter.
uncertainty: Exact authorship (Google vs community org) and release cadence beyond README.
Runtime safety of commands/scripts under .gemini and scripts/.
Whether --auto-update behavior is fully reliable.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI commands to create, modify, and commit Flutter ap
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that bootstraps Flutter/Dart projects, plans changes, and runs pre-commit checks with conventional messages.
pros: README documents Gemini CLI 0.4.0+ install, update, and uninstall plus /create-app, /create-package, /modify, and /commit commands.
Repository is public under BSD-3-Clause with CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, CHANGELOG, and gemini-extension.json.
Activity signals include ~401 stars, 27 forks, and 75 commits on main.
States experimental status and notes a known Windows install issue with a workaround.
cons: GitHub About has no description or topics; status is explicitly experimental and commands may change.
Windows installation currently fails without a documented workaround.
Facts payload was empty; deeper code quality and security of scripts were not independently audited.

aiReview.summary: Official Gemini CLI Firebase extension repo is deprecated and now only points users to firebase/agent-skills; do not list this URL as a live resource.
evidence: README title: Firebase Extension for Gemini CLI (Deprecated).
Replacement link: https://github.com/firebase/agent-skills.
GitHub shows ~124 stars, 19 forks, 13 commits, Apache-2.0, no description.
File listing is only LICENSE and README.md.
uncertainty: Current quality of firebase/agent-skills was not reviewed.
Whether Gemini CLI still accepts installs from this old URL is unverified.
Maintenance ownership beyond the README pointer is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Deprecated CLI extension; install successor agent skills ins
aiReview.description: Points Gemini CLI users to install Firebase agent skills from the replacement GitHub repository.
pros: README states deprecation and names the replacement repository firebase/agent-skills.
Provides an install command for the successor: gemini extensions install https://github.com/firebase/agent-skills.
Apache-2.0 licensed public GitHub project under gemini-cli-extensions.
cons: Repository is explicitly deprecated with no remaining product description or topics.
Only LICENSE and a short README remain; no extension source or docs to review.
Listing this URL in a directory would send users to a stub instead of the maintained project.

aiReview.summary: Google Cloud Platform Gemini CLI / agent plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s Firestore server so agents can query and manage Firestore via natural language. Official Apache-2.0 repo, still beta (pre-v1.0) with possible breaking changes.
evidence: README: packages MCP Toolbox firestore server as plugin/extension; Gemini CLI v1.6+ / Antigravity.
Topics include gemini, gemini-cli, gemini-cli-extension.
Apache-2.0; FIRESTORE_PROJECT and optional FIRESTORE_DATABASE.
Beta note: pre-v1.0 breaking changes.
uncertainty: Exact latest release version and runtime security review of MCP tools not verified.
Whether awesome-list should list redirect vs current GCP repo.
aiReview.tagline: Agent plugin for natural-language Firestore ops
aiReview.description: Install an MCP Firestore plugin for Gemini CLI and other agents to query collections and manage documents with ADC.
pros: Official GoogleCloudPlatform repository with Apache-2.0 license, changelog, and contributing docs.
Documents Gemini CLI / Antigravity install, env vars, IAM, and ADC prerequisites.
Packages MCP Toolbox’s prebuilt Firestore server with gemini-extension.json.
122 commits and a releases page; README notes beta until v1.0.
cons: Still marked beta with possible breaking changes before v1.0.
Candidate URL gemini-cli-extensions/firestore-native redirects to GoogleCloudPlatform/firestore-native-plugin.
Requires Node.js, Firestore API, ADC, and Datastore/Firebase Rules IAM.
Stars/forks are modest (~30/6) so community adoption is limited.

aiReview.summary: Official-looking Gemini CLI extension that installs an MCP server so the agent can run gcloud against the user's Google Cloud account. Preview-status thin wrapper with a command denylist; useful for Gemini CLI users, but agent-driven cloud mutations warrant caution.
evidence: GitHub description: gcloud Gemini CLI Extension; homepage points to github.com/googleapis/gcloud-mcp.
README install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/gcloud; MCP list shows npx -y @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp.
Apache-2.0, 64 stars, 6 forks, 3 commits on main.
Important notes: preview, may see breaking changes, not an officially supported Google product.
uncertainty: Cannot verify maintenance cadence beyond three commits or npm package freshness.
Cannot independently audit the denied-command list or runtime safety of gcloud-mcp.
Relationship between gemini-cli-extensions/gcloud and googleapis/gcloud-mcp ownership is inferred from docs.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI MCP extension for Google Cloud via CLI
aiReview.description: Installs an MCP server so Gemini CLI can run gcloud against your GCP account, with a denylist for unsafe commands.
pros: Installs as a Gemini CLI extension with documented gemini extensions install and mcp list verification.
Exposes a single run_gcloud_command MCP tool backed by googleapis/gcloud-mcp.
Documents a denylist of interactive or arbitrary-input gcloud commands and least-privilege impersonation guidance.
Apache-2.0 license with CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, and issue templates present.
cons: README states the repo is in preview, may break, and is not an officially supported Google product.
Only three commits and a small file set (manifest plus docs), so the extension itself is a thin wrapper.
Agent-executed gcloud inherits the active account permissions and can still mutate cloud resources.

aiReview.summary: Official-looking Gemini CLI extension that installs Genkit docs and MCP tools so the CLI can inspect, generate, and debug Genkit apps. Thin repo (13 commits, no GitHub description) but README install/usage is clear and Apache-2.0 licensed.
evidence: README title: Genkit Extension for Gemini CLI; install command and usage examples for flows/evaluators/traces.
Files include gemini-extension.json, GENKIT.md, Apache-2.0 LICENSE.
Repo is public under gemini-cli-extensions/genkit with 176 stars.
uncertainty: Exact MCP tool surface and whether it calls Gemini API directly vs Genkit runtime.
Recent commit dates and active maintainer identity beyond org name.
Runtime security of MCP tools was not audited.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI tools and docs for Genkit apps
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that adds Genkit documentation and MCP tools to build, evaluate, and debug flows.
pros: README documents install via gemini extensions install from this GitHub URL.
Describes using Genkit MCP tools plus docs for flows, evaluators, and traces.
Apache-2.0 license, contributing docs, and a gemini-extension.json manifest are present.
Public repo with 176 stars and 19 forks at review time.
cons: GitHub About has no description, website, or topics.
History is only 13 commits; maintenance depth is limited from the listing.
No releases listed on the repository page.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud Gemini CLI extension that installs MCP Toolbox so you can define tools.yaml and query custom/database-backed MCP tools from the terminal. Beta (pre-v1.0) with documented ADC and binary-download issues; still a direct, well-documented Gemini CLI integration.
evidence: README title Gemini CLI Extension - MCP Toolbox; install URL GoogleCloudPlatform/mcp-toolbox-plugin.
109 stars, 10 forks, Apache-2.0, gemini-extension.json present.
Beta warning and troubleshooting for ADC, MCP connection closed, and toolbox ENOENT.
uncertainty: Cannot verify runtime security of downloaded Toolbox binary or tools.yaml execution.
Maintenance cadence beyond 99 commits and last-commit metadata not fully inspected.
Redirect from gemini-cli-extensions/mcp-toolbox vs GoogleCloudPlatform ownership long-term.
aiReview.tagline: Query custom MCP database tools from Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension to build and invoke custom MCP tools from tools.yaml using natural language in the terminal.
pros: GoogleCloudPlatform repo with Apache-2.0 license, CONTRIBUTING, changelog, and ~99 commits.
README covers install via gemini extensions, Gemini CLI v0.6.0+, ADC, and troubleshooting.
Integrates MCP Toolbox so agents can use custom tools defined in tools.yaml.
cons: Marked beta (pre-v1.0) with possible breaking changes.
GitHub About has no description or topics; canonical gemini-cli-extensions URL redirects.
Requires database APIs, ADC, and a correctly downloaded Toolbox binary.

aiReview.summary: Community Gemini CLI extension that talks to Neo4j via env-configured credentials and Cypher tools. Small GitHub footprint (few stars/commits) and still marked beta; worth listing after a quick quality check.
evidence: GitHub about text: Neo4j extension for Gemini-CLI; Apache-2.0.
README lists list_tables and execute_cypher tools and NEO4J_URI/USER/PASSWORD.
Install command points at gemini-cli-extensions/neo4j; this fork/repo shows 3 stars and 5 commits.
uncertainty: Whether this GitHub account is the canonical upstream vs gemini-cli-extensions/neo4j.
Runtime security of Cypher execution against user databases.
Release cadence and test coverage beyond listed docs.
aiReview.tagline: Query Neo4j from Gemini CLI with Cypher tools
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension to explore Neo4j schemas, run Cypher, and generate code from graph nodes using natural language.
pros: Apache-2.0 Gemini CLI extension with documented install, env vars, and tool list.
Supports schema listing and Cypher execution plus usage examples.
Includes license, changelog, contributing, and developer docs.
cons: Repository has only a handful of commits, stars, and no forks.
README marks the extension as beta with possible breaking changes.
Database credentials are env vars and the connection cannot change mid-session.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s AlloyDB Postgres server so Gemini CLI/Antigravity (and other agents) can manage clusters and query databases via natural language. Beta (pre-v1.0), needs GCP IAM, ADC, and instance env vars.
evidence: GitHub About: Skills for AlloyDB; topics include gemini-cli and gemini-cli-extension.
README packages MCP Toolbox alloydb-postgres as a plugin; beta note and tool/lifecycle claims.
License Apache-2.0; CoC and CONTRIBUTING present.
uncertainty: Exact latest release quality and eval results not fully inspected.
Safety of agent-issued SQL/admin actions depends on user IAM and MCP server behavior.
aiReview.tagline: Agent plugin for AlloyDB Postgres via MCP Toolbox
aiReview.description: Install an MCP-backed plugin so Gemini CLI and other agents can query, schema-explore, and manage AlloyDB for PostgreSQL.
pros: GoogleCloudPlatform repo with gemini-extension.json, Apache-2.0 license, and 128 commits.
Documents install for Gemini CLI/Antigravity plus Claude Code and Codex.
Lists env vars, IAM roles, ADC, and available tools for AlloyDB operations.
Includes changelog, contributing, evals, and release-please automation.
cons: README states beta status with possible breaking changes before v1.0.
Requires a live GCP AlloyDB instance, Node/npx, and admin-capable IAM.
Canonical gemini-cli-extensions/alloydb URL redirects; stars remain low (~24).

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s Spanner server so Gemini CLI/Antigravity (and other agents) can query and manage Cloud Spanner via natural language. Relevant as a Gemini CLI extension, but still beta and not a Gemini API SDK.
evidence: README: packages MCP Toolbox prebuilt spanner server as a plugin for Antigravity/Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Codex.
Repo topics include gemini, gemini-cli, gemini-cli-extension.
Prerequisites: Gemini CLI/Antigravity versions, Node.js npx MCP, Spanner API, ADC, databaseReader/databaseUser roles.
License Apache-2.0; beta note at top of README.
uncertainty: Live extension quality and tool list beyond README first page.
Whether gemini-cli-extensions/spanner remains the stable canonical URL.
Production stability of MCP Toolbox Spanner server integration.
aiReview.tagline: Natural-language Spanner access for Gemini CLI agents
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI/Antigravity plugin that talks to Cloud Spanner via MCP Toolbox to explore schemas, run queries, and generate code.
pros: Hosted under GoogleCloudPlatform with Apache-2.0, CONTRIBUTING, CoC, changelog, and 121 commits.
Documents Gemini CLI/Antigravity install, env vars, IAM roles, and ADC prerequisites.
Includes gemini-extension.json plus MCP config for agent integration.
States beta/pre-v1.0 status and points to a releases page.
cons: Canonical listing URL gemini-cli-extensions/spanner redirects to GoogleCloudPlatform/spanner-plugin.
Marked beta with possible breaking changes until v1.0.
Stars are low (19) and the plugin also targets Claude Code and Codex, not Gemini-only.
Database access depends on GCP credentials and Spanner IAM, so misconfiguration can expose data.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s Cloud SQL for MySQL server for Gemini CLI / Antigravity and other agents. Beta (pre-v1.0) with solid docs, IAM/env-var setup, and Apache-2.0; still early stars and possible breaking changes.
evidence: GitHub About: Skills for Cloud SQL for MySQL; topics include gemini, gemini-cli, gemini-cli-extension.
README: packages MCP Toolbox prebuilt cloud-sql-mysql server; beta note; Gemini CLI v1.6+ / Antigravity 2.0.
License Apache-2.0; files include gemini-extension.json, mcp.json, CLOUD-SQL-MYSQL.md.
uncertainty: Exact latest release version and eval quality not fully inspected.
Runtime security of MCP DB tools against destructive queries not audited.
aiReview.tagline: Natural-language Cloud SQL MySQL tools for AI agents
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI / agent plugin that queries Cloud SQL for MySQL, explores schemas, and manages instances via MCP Toolbox.
pros: GoogleCloudPlatform Apache-2.0 repo with gemini-extension.json, MCP configs, and Gemini CLI / Antigravity install paths.
README documents env vars, IAM roles, ADC, and natural-language DB lifecycle/query use.
115 commits, changelog, contributing, evals, and release-please indicate active maintenance.
Also supports Claude Code and Codex, not Gemini-only.
cons: Marked beta (pre-v1.0) with possible breaking changes.
Low adoption signals (about 12 stars, 2 forks).
Canonical listing URL gemini-cli-extensions/cloud-sql-mysql redirects to GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-mysql-plugin.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s cloud-sql-postgres server so Gemini CLI / Antigravity (and other agents) can manage Cloud SQL PostgreSQL via natural language. Beta (pre-v1.0) with real IAM/credential and query-execution surface; docs and maintenance look solid.
evidence: GitHub about: Skills for Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL; topics include gemini, gemini-cli, gemini-cli-extension.
README: wraps MCP Toolbox cloud-sql-postgres; requires Cloud SQL Admin API, ADC, Cloud SQL Client/Admin roles.
Repo has 156 commits, Apache-2.0, gemini-extension.json, mcp.json, evals, release-please.
uncertainty: Runtime security of MCP Toolbox tools and eval coverage of destructive queries not audited here.
Star/fork counts are modest (42/7); long-term CLI vs Antigravity branding may keep shifting.
aiReview.tagline: Agent plugin for Cloud SQL PostgreSQL via MCP
aiReview.description: Install an MCP-backed agent plugin to manage Cloud SQL PostgreSQL instances, schemas, and queries from Gemini CLI and similar agents.
pros: Hosted under GoogleCloudPlatform with gemini-extension.json, Apache-2.0, changelog, contributing, and evals.
Documents env vars, ADC/IAM roles, IP types, and install paths for Gemini CLI/Antigravity, Claude Code, and Codex.
Packages MCP Toolbox’s prebuilt cloud-sql-postgres server rather than an undocumented custom protocol.
cons: README states the project is beta (pre-v1.0) and may break until a stable release.
Agents can run database operations; misconfigured IAM or env credentials increase operational risk.
Canonical listing URL redirects to a different GitHub org/repo name than gemini-cli-extensions/cloud-sql-postgresql.
