aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s cloud-sql-mssql server so Gemini CLI/Antigravity (and other agents) can manage Cloud SQL for SQL Server via natural language. Beta (pre-v1.0), Apache-2.0, documented install and IAM/env setup; canonical URL redirects from gemini-cli-extensions to GoogleCloudPlatform.
evidence: GitHub description: Skills for Cloud SQL for SQL Server; topics include gemini, gemini-cli, gemini-cli-extension.
README packages MCP Toolbox prebuilt cloud-sql-mssql for Antigravity, Claude Code, and Codex.
Candidate URL https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/cloud-sql-sqlserver resolves to GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-sqlserver-plugin.
License Apache-2.0; 104 commits on main.
uncertainty: Live tool behavior and MCP server security posture were not executed.
Whether gemini-cli-extensions remains a maintained alias vs only the GCP org repo.
aiReview.tagline: Agent plugin to query and manage Cloud SQL SQL Server
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI/Antigravity plugin that uses MCP Toolbox to explore schemas, run queries, and administer Cloud SQL for SQL Server.
pros: Ships gemini-extension.json and documents Gemini CLI/Antigravity install, including migration from gemini extensions install.
Apache-2.0 GoogleCloudPlatform repo with changelog, contributing docs, evals, and release-please.
Lists prerequisites (ADC, Cloud SQL Admin API, IAM roles) and env vars for data-plane vs admin tools.
cons: README states the extension is beta (pre-v1.0) and may break until a stable release.
Database credentials and optional IP type are configured via environment variables, which needs careful handling.

aiReview.summary: Official Elastic Gemini CLI extension that talks to Elasticsearch via MCP (Agent Builder) and optional Agent Skills; experimental but documented with install, env vars, tools, and troubleshooting.
evidence: GitHub description: Official Elasticsearch extension for Gemini CLI.
README: gemini extensions install https://github.com/elastic/gemini-cli-elasticsearch; MCP tools and /elastic:* commands.
Apache-2.0 LICENSE; experimental caution in README.
Repo stats from GitHub: public, ~118 stars, 3 forks, 58 commits.
uncertainty: Runtime quality of MCP against live Elastic clusters not verified.
Exact last-commit date and release cadence beyond 58 commits not inspected in git log.
Elasticsearch/Kibana licensing for production clusters is separate from this repo.
aiReview.tagline: Search and analyze Elasticsearch from Gemini CLI via MCP
aiReview.description: Install an official Gemini CLI extension to list indices, search, map fields, and run ES|QL against Elasticsearch through MCP.
pros: Official Elastic repo with Apache-2.0 license, README, GEMINI.md, gemini-extension.json, and a security policy.
Documents gemini extensions install, ELASTIC_URL/ELASTIC_MCP_URL/ELASTIC_API_KEY, MCP tool list, slash commands, and troubleshooting.
Exposes Agent Builder MCP tools (search, mappings, ES|QL generate/execute) plus optional skills.js Agent Skills.
Active history (58 commits on main) and public GitHub presence (~118 stars).
cons: README marks the extension as experimental.
Requires Elastic Serverless or 9.3+ Agent Builder MCP URL plus an encoded API key, so setup is cluster-specific.
Stars/forks are modest; MCP connectivity quality depends on the user’s Elastic deployment.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud Platform Gemini CLI extension (also Claude/Codex/Antigravity) that talks to MySQL via an MCP server, including schema exploration and arbitrary SQL. Docs are clear; it is still beta and execute_sql plus stored credentials are a real ops/safety consideration.
evidence: README title: Gemini CLI Extension - MySQL; install via gemini extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/mysql.
Supported tools listed: list_tables, execute_sql, get_query_plan, list_active_queries, index/fragmentation helpers.
Repo GoogleCloudPlatform/mysql-plugin: Apache-2.0, ~81 commits, ~42 stars, gemini-extension.json present.
uncertainty: Runtime security review of the MCP server and @toolbox-sdk/server was not performed.
Current release version and last-commit recency were not verified beyond README beta note.
aiReview.tagline: Natural-language MySQL tools for Gemini CLI via MCP
aiReview.description: Query schemas, run SQL, and inspect MySQL from Gemini CLI and other agent harnesses using an npx MCP server.
pros: Google-maintained repo with Apache-2.0 license, changelog, and install paths for Gemini CLI.
README documents env vars, troubleshooting, and tools including list_tables, execute_sql, and query-plan helpers.
MCP server runs via npx with no separate binary download.
cons: Marked beta (pre-v1.0) with possible breaking changes.
execute_sql can run any SQL the configured user is allowed to run.
Connection cannot be changed mid-session; password is stored in env or extension .env.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud Gemini CLI extension (beta) that talks to PostgreSQL via MCP/npx so you can query, inspect schemas, and generate code from natural language. Direct Gemini CLI relevance is high; it is pre-v1.0 with DB credentials in env, so treat it as a reviewed listing rather than a generic SDK.
evidence: README title: Gemini CLI Extension - PostgreSQL; install via gemini extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/postgres.
Repo files: gemini-extension.json, mcp.json, Apache-2.0, 96 stars, 13 forks.
Prerequisites: Gemini CLI v0.6.0+, Node.js/npx MCP server, database-level query permissions.
uncertainty: Exact MCP tool list and query safety (read-only vs write) not fully verified from truncated README.
Maintenance cadence and security review of credential handling not independently audited.
Whether gemini-cli-extensions/postgres remains the stable install URL long-term.
aiReview.tagline: Natural-language Postgres tools inside Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Query PostgreSQL, inspect schemas, and generate code from Gemini CLI using an MCP server and env-based connection settings.
pros: README documents Gemini CLI install, config, and PostgreSQL env vars with Apache-2.0 licensing.
Includes gemini-extension.json, MCP configs, changelog, and ~100 commits under GoogleCloudPlatform.
Supports Gemini CLI plus Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity with the same plugin.
Beta note and feedback form are explicit about pre-v1.0 breakage.
cons: GitHub About has no description; canonical URL redirects from gemini-cli-extensions/postgres to GoogleCloudPlatform/postgres-plugin.
Extension is beta and may break before v1.0.

The page enumerates many named tools covering contacts, campaigns, enrichment, and account audit.
FAQ states MCP access is included in the platform plan and notes rate limits and send confirmations.
cons: No Gemini API, Gemini CLI, or Google AI setup is documented; examples center on Claude.
Functionality is LinkedIn sales automation, which may conflict with LinkedIn terms of use.
Requires a paid/trial LinkedNav workspace; not an open-source SDK or tutorial.

aiReview.summary: Hosted LinkedIn MCP for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and n8n with no Gemini API or Gemini CLI integration; LinkedIn ToS risk from automated messaging and invites.
evidence: Page title and meta describe a hosted LinkedIn MCP for Claude, ChatGPT, and n8n, not Gemini.
MCP URL https://api.heyreagent.com/mcp with OAuth or Bearer key depending on client.
Claims 97 actions; free vs Connect vs Agent pricing and daily invite/message/comment caps.
FAQ: not affiliated with LinkedIn; automation can lead to account restriction.
uncertainty: Cannot verify actual MCP tool quality, uptime, or LinkedIn session handling without signing in.
Cannot verify GitHub star claim for the compared local LinkedIn MCP.
Gemini CLI listing context is only the README anchor, not product docs.
aiReview.tagline: Hosted LinkedIn MCP for chat apps and n8n
aiReview.description: Paste a remote MCP URL so AI apps can read inbox, message, invite, and search on your LinkedIn account.
pros: Documents a single remote MCP endpoint and setup steps for Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, Muse, and n8n.
Lists action categories, daily rate limits, and pricing (free live use, Connect $29.99/mo, Agent $499/mo).
States it is unofficial and that LinkedIn may restrict accounts for automated activity.
cons: No Gemini API, AI Studio, or Gemini CLI usage is described; listing is only via awesome-gemini-cli.
Automates LinkedIn messaging, invitations, and search, which LinkedIn’s User Agreement disallows.
Free plan disconnects LinkedIn after idle time, so scheduled workflows need a paid plan.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that installs two slash commands and a hosted MCP client for searching unofficial Grok Bot Wiki templates and troubleshooting guides. Docs are clear on install, consent, and that the remote service is read-only and unaffiliated with xAI or Google.
evidence: GitHub description and README: read-only Grok Bot Wiki MCP tools for Gemini CLI.
Install path: gemini extensions install https://github.com/SeleemS/grokbotwiki-gemini-extension.
MCP listed as https://www.grokbotwiki.com/api/mcp; topics include gemini-cli-extension.
uncertainty: Actual gemini-extension.json and command prompt contents were not fully inspected beyond the README listing.
Cannot verify hosted MCP security, uptime, or data handling beyond the stated privacy policy link.
VALIDATION.md dated checks were not read in full.
aiReview.tagline: Read-only wiki search for Grok bot templates in CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that queries a hosted MCP for community Grok bot listings and source-linked troubleshooting guides.
pros: README documents Gemini CLI install, MCP endpoint, and two slash commands.
States the extension is unofficial, read-only, and does not run or modify Grok bots.
MIT license, GEMINI.md, and gemini-extension.json are present; no local shell/install hooks claimed.
cons: Repository is very new (2 commits, 2 stars) with little independent maintenance evidence.
Tool queries go to a third-party hosted MCP at grokbotwiki.com, so availability and content quality depend on that service.
Listed templates are described as untested public share pages.

aiReview.summary: Windows desktop harness that embeds Gemini CLI among other coding agents on a widget canvas; Gemini is one of several vendor CLIs, not a first-party Gemini API resource.
evidence: Meta description and FAQ name Gemini CLI/Cursor/Claude/Codex widgets and a free VF- license with no harness subscription.
FAQ states VibeFuse is not open source; it wraps vendor CLIs.
Listed on Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README with only the product name as surrounding text.
uncertainty: No source repo, changelog quality, or actual Gemini API usage to inspect.
Installer, key gating, marketplace payouts, and Google OAuth MCP security not independently verified.
Maintenance cadence beyond claimed v1.1.0 is unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Windows canvas for coding CLIs, widgets, and local voice
aiReview.description: Free Windows desktop that tiles terminals, browsers, and coding CLIs including Gemini, with local voice, MCP, and a widget marketplace.
pros: Documents Gemini CLI as one of several side-by-side coding-agent widgets on a Windows canvas.
Lists a Settings → Agent Google Gemini provider card among other OpenAI-compatible backends.
Public FAQ and docs cover install, architecture (C:\vibefuse\), MCP, and marketplace widgets.
cons: The harness itself is not open source; it wraps third-party CLIs behind a closed Windows installer and VF- license key.
Gemini API/SDK implementation quality cannot be verified from marketing pages alone.
Page is heavily comparative marketing versus Grok Bot and Perplexity Computer rather than Gemini-focused docs.

aiReview.summary: ReadTheDocs page for IssueDB CLI LLM-agent usage (JSON output, --prompt, Ollama). It targets generic assistants and Ollama, not the Gemini API, so it is a weak fit for a Gemini developer directory.
evidence: Page title and overview: LLM Agent Integration for IssueDB CLI.
Native LLM path is Ollama (llama3.2/codellama), not Gemini.
Claude Code system-prompt example is the primary assistant walkthrough.
Listed in awesome-gemini-cli as IssueDB pointing at this docs URL.
uncertainty: Whether issuedb-cli is open-source, maintained, or how it is licensed.
Whether any unpublished Gemini support exists outside this page.
Live CLI behavior versus documentation (command spacing in the rendered page).
aiReview.tagline: CLI issue tracker with JSON and Ollama agent hooks
aiReview.description: Documents issuedb-cli agent prompts, Ollama natural-language flags, JSON automation, and sample Claude/CI patterns.
pros: Documents machine-readable --json output and a built-in --prompt for agent system instructions.
Covers Ollama setup, environment variables, and example natural-language commands.
Includes agent command patterns for create, query, update, bulk ops, and a GitHub Actions sketch.
cons: No Gemini API, Gemini CLI, or Google AI integration is described.
Examples center on Claude, GPT, and Ollama rather than Gemini.
HTML extraction shows concatenated CLI tokens, which may reduce copy-paste reliability.

aiReview.summary: Hosted MCP and HTTP intel layer for x402 agent payments (Solana/Base), not a Gemini API SDK. Extensive docs exist, but Gemini-directory fit is weak and paid crypto settlement plus wallet-key MCP configs raise review risk.
evidence: Canonical URL returns MCP_USE_POST_STREAMABLE_HTTP JSON pointing at POST initialize and .well-known/mcp.json.
llms.txt states TWZRD is a pre-spend trust gate for x402/Solana, npm twzrd-x402-gate@0.12.0, service v0.5.13.
MCP card lists 28 free tools, paid HTTP surfaces, Smithery listing, and github.com/twzrd-sol/twzrd-trust.
Discovered only as an awesome-gemini-cli README link with UTM referral, not Gemini-specific docs.
uncertainty: Live Gemini CLI plugin quality and whether the awesome list section is MCP-generic vs Gemini-specific.
Independence and accuracy of wash/reputation scoring versus on-chain reality.
Current health of market-data tools and whether npm/PyPI packages match documented versions.
aiReview.tagline: Pre-spend x402 trust checks and signed receipts for agents
aiReview.description: Score sellers before x402 spends via free MCP/HTTP preflight, optional paid receipts, and a client gate that can refuse signing.
pros: Documents a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at /mcp with free preflight, merchant-card, and receipt-verify tools.
Public llms.txt, OpenAPI, MCP card, and GitHub packages describe allow/warn/block semantics and a buyer-side refuse-before-sign hook.
Free advisory HTTP/MCP paths are separated from optional paid x402 routes (e.g. 0.001 USDC /quick, 0.05 USDC V7 receipts).
cons: No Gemini API, AI Studio, or Gemini CLI integration is described; the listing is payment-trust infrastructure.
Local auto-pay MCP config asks for a Solana wallet secret and spend caps, which is easy to misconfigure.
Free preflight is explicitly advisory until a client gate honors block; market-data routes are currently unlisted/410.

aiReview.summary: HTTP MCP server that lets assistants search a public AI-tools catalog; useful as a client integration, but it is not a Gemini API or Gemini CLI resource.
evidence: Page title and meta describe a free, no-auth MCP server at https://aisotools.com/api/mcp.
Setup snippets use claude mcp add --transport http and JSON mcpServers type http.
Tools named: search_ai_tools, get_ai_tool, list_ai_tool_categories, compare_ai_tools, find_ai_tool_alternatives.
Discovered as 'AISO Tools MCP' in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README with utm_source=awesome-gemini-cli.
uncertainty: Could not verify live MCP handshake, tool schemas, or catalog accuracy from this review.
Open-source status of the server implementation is not stated.
Gemini CLI compatibility is inferred only from being listed in that awesome README.
aiReview.tagline: Unauthenticated MCP access to a public AI-tools catalog
aiReview.description: Query a curated AI-tools directory over MCP with five read-only tools, no API key, via streamable HTTP.
pros: Documents a public HTTP MCP endpoint with setup for Claude Code, Desktop, Cursor, and stdio via mcp-remote.
Lists five read-only tools with argument shapes and response behaviors (matched counts, unmatched names, sponsored flags).
States no API key, POST-only/stateless limits, and that catalog data is not live vendor pricing.
cons: No Gemini API, Gemini CLI, or Google AI implementation content on the page.
Catalog freshness and alternative quality depend on a third-party directory, not vendor sources.
The listing URL includes a referral UTM from an awesome list.

aiReview.summary: Datacircle is a comparison catalog of LinkedIn/GTM scraping and enrichment APIs, not a Gemini API, CLI, or SDK resource. The listed MCP-server docs URL resolves to that catalog, so it is a poor fit for an awesome Gemini list.
evidence: Fetched https://docs.datacircle.dev/mcp-server which resolved to datacircle.dev describing LinkedIn profile API plans and GTM API comparison sheets.
Page lists dozens of third-party scrapers/enrichers (Apify, Bright Data, Hunter, etc.) with no Gemini API mention.
FAQ: Datacircle is a sheet of GTM APIs; signup required to download CSV/JSON/zip.
uncertainty: Whether an MCP server page exists at a different path; this fetch did not show MCP or Gemini CLI setup.
Accuracy of catalog pricing rows was not independently verified.
License/open-source status of the catalog itself is unclear.
aiReview.tagline: Compare LinkedIn and GTM enrichment API pricing
aiReview.description: Compare LinkedIn, email, phone, and company GTM APIs by cost, freshness, limits, and returned fields.
pros: Publishes a large spreadsheet-style catalog of GTM/LinkedIn-related APIs with cost, freshness, rate-limit, and field columns.
Offers CSV, JSON, and zip downloads plus an archive dated 14 October 2026.
States numbers come from each provider’s pricing pages and docs.
Says it does not sell people data; it lists third-party APIs.
cons: Canonical MCP-server docs URL does not describe Gemini, Gemini CLI, or Google AI integration.
Content is a lead-enrichment/scraping catalog, which is off-topic for a Gemini developer directory.
Downloads require work-email signup; Gemini/MCP usage is not documented on the fetched page.

aiReview.summary: Hosted LinkedIn sales MCP server for Claude and other MCP clients; it is not a Gemini API or Gemini CLI resource and mainly sells outreach automation.
evidence: Canonical page title and copy: LinkedIn MCP Server for AI Assistants; setup uses Claude Connectors.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README as LinkedNav with a UTM referral URL.
FAQ claims any MCP client including Cursor/VS Code; Gemini is not named.
uncertainty: Cannot verify actual Gemini CLI compatibility or tool quality without connecting.
LinkedIn ToS compliance and real sending behavior are unverified.
Full plan pricing is only linked, not quoted on the MCP page.
aiReview.tagline: MCP tools for LinkedIn lists, campaigns, and enrichment
aiReview.description: Connect an MCP client with a URL and API key to search leads, run LinkedIn campaigns, enrich contacts, and query results in natural language.
pros: Documents a hosted MCP endpoint at https://mcp.linkednav.com with step-by-step Claude connector setup.
Lists grouped tools for contacts, campaigns, enrichment, senders, and workspace admin.
States MCP access is included in the platform plan and notes rate limits and API-key scoped access.
cons: Page targets Claude, Cursor, and generic MCP clients; it does not mention Gemini or the Gemini API.
Product is LinkedIn outreach automation, which may conflict with LinkedIn terms of use.
Pricing beyond a 7-day trial is not specified on this page.

aiReview.summary: Hosted LinkedIn MCP for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and n8n—not a Gemini API resource. Automation may violate LinkedIn terms; treat as off-scope for a Gemini directory.
evidence: Page title and meta describe a LinkedIn MCP for Claude, ChatGPT, and n8n, not Gemini.
MCP URL https://api.heyreagent.com/mcp with OAuth or Bearer key depending on client.
Pricing: Free $0 (session drops after idle), Connect $29.99/mo, Agent $499/mo.
FAQ admits LinkedIn does not allow automated activity and that limits do not remove that risk.
Candidate source is Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README with only the product name as anchor.
uncertainty: Cannot verify actual MCP tool quality, uptime, or data handling beyond the marketing page.
Cannot verify LinkedIn ToS enforcement outcomes or security of stored sessions.
No GitHub repo or Gemini-specific docs found on this page.
aiReview.tagline: Hosted LinkedIn MCP for chat apps and n8n
aiReview.description: Paste one MCP URL so AI apps can read your LinkedIn inbox, message, invite, and search. Free to start; paid plans keep the session.
pros: Documents a remote MCP endpoint with setup steps for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code, Muse, and n8n.
Lists many LinkedIn actions, daily rate limits, and free versus paid plan differences.
States it is unofficial and that LinkedIn may restrict automated use.
No local install; session is hosted after connecting your own account.
cons: No Gemini API, Gemini CLI, or Google AI integration is described.
LinkedIn automation can breach LinkedIn’s user agreement and risk account restriction.
Free plan disconnects LinkedIn after idle time; persistent use is paid.
Discovery is a UTM affiliate link from an awesome-gemini-cli list, not a Gemini SDK.

aiReview.summary: The listed GitHub repository returns 404 and has no readable README or source, so it cannot be verified as a Gemini CLI extension or developer resource.
evidence: GitHub HTML fetch failed with HTTP 404.
raw.githubusercontent.com/.../main/README.md also failed with HTTP 404.
Candidate metadata only cites awesome-list anchor text 'Warmerly' with no facts.readme or excerpt.
Web search did not surface a public warmerlyapp/gemini-extension repository.
uncertainty: Whether the repo is private, renamed, deleted, or never published.
What Warmerly actually does, pricing, and license.
Whether it uses the Gemini API or only Gemini CLI extension hooks.
pros: It was linked from a curated Gemini CLI extensions list under the name Warmerly.
The URL path suggests a Gemini CLI extension rather than an unrelated product.
cons: https://github.com/warmerlyapp/gemini-extension currently returns HTTP 404.
No README, license, stars, or implementation details could be retrieved.
Maintenance, documentation quality, and safety cannot be assessed.

aiReview.summary: Official Google blog announcing Gemini 4 Argon in the Antigravity desktop app, CLI, and Gemini platform API for Pro, Ultra, and eligible Enterprise subscribers. Useful as a product/availability notice, not as implementation docs or SDK reference.
evidence: canonical URL https://antigravity.google/blog/gemini-4-argon-in-google-antigravity/
Title and body: Gemini 4 Argon rolling out in Antigravity for Google AI Pro and Ultra, desktop app and CLI.
Business availability via API in Gemini platform and Antigravity on eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions.
Getting started section points to download, Google AI plans, and Cloud Gemini Enterprise docs.
uncertainty: Cannot independently verify internal Alphabet usage statistics or case-study outcomes.
Exact model ID strings and API endpoints are not listed on this page.
Pricing tier details beyond Pro/Ultra/Enterprise eligibility are not specified here.
aiReview.tagline: Frontier model rollout for agent-first desktop and CLI work
aiReview.description: Announces a new frontier model in an agent-first desktop app, CLI, and platform API for Pro, Ultra, and eligible Enterprise plans.
pros: Official antigravity.google blog post dated Oct 13, 2026 with clear availability channels (desktop app, CLI, Gemini platform API).
States access for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers plus eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions.
Links to the Gemini 4 Argon model announcement, Google AI plans, and Gemini Enterprise developer-tools docs.
Describes agentic engineering, localization, finance, and sales workflows with plugins, skills, and MCP integrations.
cons: Marketing case studies and internal metrics, not API reference, code samples, or integration tutorials.
Does not document model IDs, request formats, rate limits, or migration steps for existing Gemini API users.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Gemini CLI extension that points at a hosted PostEverywhere MCP server so users can draft, schedule, and publish social posts from Gemini CLI; it needs a PostEverywhere account (plan or trial) and has no GitHub traction yet.
evidence: Repo description and README: Gemini CLI plugin for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X and more via hosted MCP, no local API key.
Install command: gemini extensions install https://github.com/posteverywhere/gemini-cli-extension.
README: first-time browser sign-in; account with plan or free trial required.
License: MIT; stars/forks/issues all 0.
Privacy section: plugin ships instructions and MCP address only; traffic goes to mcp.posteverywhere.ai over HTTPS.
uncertainty: Actual MCP tool quality, uptime, and auth security cannot be verified from the repo listing.
PostEverywhere pricing tiers and trial terms were not inspected beyond the pricing link mention.
Whether gemini-extension.json and skills match current Gemini CLI extension schema was not independently validated.
aiReview.tagline: Schedule and publish social posts from Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that talks to a hosted MCP server to draft, schedule, and publish posts across major social networks.
pros: README documents install via gemini extensions install, browser sign-in, and the hosted MCP URL.
Lists 15 skills covering scheduling, calendars, analytics, failed posts, and multi-network publishing.
States tools are annotated read-only or destructive and that posts can be saved as drafts until approval.
Repository is MIT-licensed and contains skills plus gemini-extension.json rather than local runtime code.
cons: GitHub shows 0 stars, 0 forks, and 0 issues, so maintenance and adoption are unverified.
Using the extension requires a PostEverywhere account with a paid plan or active free trial.
Publishing depends on a third-party hosted MCP (mcp.posteverywhere.ai), not the Gemini API itself.

aiReview.summary: Latchkey docs for an MCP server that lets coding agents pull CI failure bundles, optionally re-run workflows, and run billed one-off jobs. Useful agent/CI tooling, but not a Gemini API or Gemini CLI resource.
evidence: Page title and body describe Latchkey MCP at https://latchkey.dev/mcp for Claude Code, Cursor, and any MCP client.
Capabilities include list failed runs, get failure bundle, tail logs, workflow_dispatch, and one-off jobs billed as runner minutes.
Security section: workspace-scoped keys, shown once, read-only by default, mcp:dispatch / jobs:run / secrets:write opt-in.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README as a Latchkey link with UTM, not Gemini-specific content.
uncertainty: Whether Latchkey is open source.
Exact pricing tiers beyond free-minute pool and billed runner minutes.
Any actual Gemini or Google AI support not mentioned on this page.
aiReview.tagline: MCP access to CI failures, re-runs, and one-off jobs
aiReview.description: Connect MCP agents to workspace-scoped keys so they can triage CI failures, fetch logs, and opt into dispatch or billed runner jobs.
pros: Documents an HTTP MCP endpoint with bearer lk_live_ keys and explicit Claude Code/Cursor setup.
Lists tools for failed runs, failure bundles, logs, triage, and guided fix flows.
Keys default to read-only; dispatch, job run, and secrets write are separate opt-ins with revocation guidance.
Points to OpenAPI, MCP manifest, agent.txt, and markdown twins of docs pages.
cons: No Gemini API, Gemini CLI, or Google AI integration is described.
Jobs-enabled keys can spend runner minutes; dispatch keys can trigger any dispatchable workflow including deploys.
The listing is a commercial product docs page, not an open Gemini developer sample.

aiReview.summary: Third-party explainer of Gemini CLI request quotas, Code Assist vs API-key billing, and cited token prices. Useful as a snapshot, but seat prices are unverified and numbers can drift from Google’s docs.
evidence: Page title and H1 cover Gemini CLI limits and pricing with tables for plans and Gemini API token rates.
Meta description and body cite 1,500/2,000 requests per user per day and docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/quotas, last verified 2026-10-13.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README as “Gemini CLI limits & pricing (QuotaBurn)” with a referral UTM.
FAQ restates cost, daily limit, and free-tier discontinuation claims.
uncertainty: Accuracy of listed model names and scheduled price-doubling dates versus live Google pricing pages.
Whether the personal free-tier discontinuation date is independently confirmed.
Site ownership, update cadence after 2026-10-13, and any affiliate relationships beyond the UTM link.
aiReview.tagline: Unofficial Gemini CLI quota and token-price snapshot
aiReview.description: Summarizes Gemini CLI daily request quotas, Code Assist vs API-key billing, and cited per-token prices with source dates.
pros: Explains that Gemini CLI counts model requests, not user prompts, and that one prompt can consume several requests.
States Code Assist agent-mode shared daily quotas (1,500 Standard / 2,000 Enterprise) and cites Google Cloud quota docs with a verification date.
Separates unverified Code Assist seat prices from API-key per-token pricing tables.
Notes the reported discontinuation of the personal free tier versus what GitHub README still advertises.
cons: It is not official Google documentation; quota and price figures can go stale.
Code Assist Standard and Enterprise seat prices are explicitly unverified and omitted.
Includes commercial comparison and newsletter CTAs typical of an aggregator site.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that runs local read-only checks on proposed file writes and Linux commands, then sends sanitized command metadata to a GOL server that may block the action. Proprietary, 0 stars, paid after 100 free blocks, and Windows command checking is not supported.
evidence: README: gemini extensions install https://github.com/golproductions/check-gemini
README: checks file writes everywhere and commands on Linux; Windows commands not checked
README: GOL API key, 100 free blocks then A$0.10 when it stops something
README: sends command (credentials stripped) to https://triage.golproductions.com
GitHub: 0 stars, 0 forks, 4 commits, proprietary licence
uncertainty: Cannot verify hook implementation quality or actual data redaction without a full code audit
Cannot verify GOL API uptime, pricing enforcement, or privacy claims
open-source tag is a poor fit; listed only because allowed tags omit proprietary
aiReview.tagline: Local pre-run checks for Gemini CLI agent actions
aiReview.description: Verify Gemini CLI file writes and Linux commands locally, then let a remote triage service stop invalid actions.
pros: Installs as a Gemini CLI extension and documents hook behavior in a short README.
Describes local read-only checks (path/program lookup, parsers) without executing the AI command.
Documents what is sent to triage.golproductions.com and fail-open behavior without a key or network.
cons: License is proprietary despite a public GitHub repo; not an open-source SDK.
Zero stars/forks and only four commits, so maintenance and community signals are weak.
Sends command text and paths to a third-party server; Windows commands are not checked.

aiReview.summary: CurlShot’s agent guide documents an MCP screenshot API (tools, quotas, caching) with clear examples; it is a third-party web-capture service, not a Gemini API or Gemini CLI resource.
evidence: Page title and content: Using the API from AI agents; POST https://curlshot.com/api/mcp JSON-RPC tools/call take_screenshot.
GitHub MCP server linked as github.com/SergiuPogor/curlshot-mcp; pricing.md and usage-and-limits.md referenced.
Candidate listed from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README as CurlShot only; no Gemini-specific APIs in the guide.
uncertainty: Current plan prices, free-tier limits, and whether video formats are included.
Maintenance cadence of the MCP server and API beyond this docs snapshot.
Why it was curated for awesome-gemini-cli given no Gemini mention.
aiReview.tagline: MCP endpoint for agents to capture page screenshots
aiReview.description: Call take_screenshot over MCP JSON-RPC, with machine-readable docs, size and cache tips, and quota handling.
pros: Documents an HTTP MCP endpoint with initialize, tools/list, and tools/call examples.
Specifies take_screenshot and list_devices arguments, MCP-specific defaults, and error/quota behavior.
Points agents at llms.txt, OpenAPI, markdown docs, and MCP/API catalog files.
cons: No Gemini API, AI Studio, or Gemini CLI integration is described.
Paid screenshot quota and access keys are required for capture; pricing is not on this page.
Screenshots of arbitrary URLs can leak content into model context if keys or pages are mishandled.

aiReview.summary: AltoRank is an SEO/content platform with MCP, REST, and CLI agent APIs; Gemini CLI is only mentioned as a skill-install target, not as a Gemini API implementation.
evidence: Page title and meta describe MCP server and agent API for ChatGPT, Claude, and Claude Code.
Skill install command: npx skills add AltoRank/altorank targeting Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, or Cline.
Hosted MCP at https://app.altorank.co/api/mcp with OAuth PKCE; REST at /api/agent/v1.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README as AltoRank with UTM referral.
uncertainty: Cannot verify GitHub activity, license details, or whether the MCP server is production-stable.
Cannot verify Gemini CLI skill quality beyond the docs mention.
Paid plan limits and drafting quota amounts are not specified on this page.
aiReview.tagline: MCP and REST APIs to audit sites and draft SEO content

States humans set architecture and verification gates while agents implemented and tested code.

FarArray and the TPU kernels are internal capabilities; the post is not a public API reference.
Performance claims are self-reported internal benchmarks.
